          as events: when each starts, how long it lasts, which register it sits in.

              frame("projection", 100, 700, 960, 270)

                  stroke(curve, name = "curve ${i + 1}", stroke = colors[i])

              println("${crossings.size} crossings along the line:")
              crossings.forEach { println("  ${it.mark.name}  %.2f of the way along".format(it.value)) }
          }

          notation.lines.lastOrNull { it.handDrawn }?.let(::read)
          notation.onChange("fontana") { edit ->
              (edit.added + edit.updated).lastOrNull { it.kind == MarkType.LINE }?.let(::read)
          }
  - create:
      box: dn_crescendo
      name: crescendo
      frame: { x: 960.0, y: 1060.0, w: 190.0, h: 60.0 }
      properties:
        code: |

                  (0..60).map { i ->
                      val k = if (i <= 30) i else 60 - i // out along the top, back along the bottom
                      val side = if (i <= 30) -1 else 1
                      vec(860 - k * 23.0, 1160 + side * (75 - k * 2.5) + hand(i))
                  }
              stroke(hairpin, name = "hairpin", stroke = "#e03131")
          }
          val dynamics = notation.space("dynamics", x = 0.0..8.0, y = 0.0..1.0)
          val markings = ["niente", "pp", "p", "mp", "mf", "f", "ff"]
          fun read() =
              (0..7).forEach { beat ->
                  val ys = dynamics.vertical(beat.toDouble()).filter { !it.isSpan }.map { it.value }
                  val gap = if (ys.size >= 2) ys.max() - ys.min() else 0.0
                  println("beat $beat: %.2f %s".format(gap, markings[(gap / 0.75 * 6).roundToInt().coerceIn(0, 6)]))
              }
          read()
          notation.onStroke("crescendo") { read() }
  - execute:
      box: dn_draw
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: dn_listen
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: dn_projection
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: dn_fontana
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: dn_read
      property: code

before:
name: drawn_score
description: >
  A drawn score, heard: four boxes that draw a score on the document's drawing, read it as notes,
  play it, and listen back to what was played. Press Alt+D to draw on it yourself.

  Run `score` first: it draws a frame named "score", a piano roll of blue rectangles, a red
  glissando and a green held note. `read` reads the frame as eight beats of MIDI pitch
  (notation.space) and prints its events. `play` decides, in a dozen lines you can edit, what each
  event means as notes (a rectangle or level line is one note, a moving stroke is cut every eighth
  of a beat), makes a pattern of them with patTimed, and renders two cycles offline into an audio
  player. `pentatonic` reads the same drawing again, snapped to C minor pentatonic. `listen back`
  finds the onsets and pitches in both renders and plots what was heard against what was drawn.
  Draw more rectangles or strokes inside the frame (Alt+D, then R or P), and run the boxes after
  `score` again.

  Companion to public/docs/chain_drawn_score.md. Pure CPU; no Window, no Renderer, no audio device.
operations:
  - create:
      box: ds_score
      name: score
      frame: { x: 20.0, y: 40.0, w: 190.0, h: 60.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          The score, drawn from code into the document's drawing: a frame named "score", a piano
          roll, a glissando and a held note. Running it again replaces these marks; anything you
          draw by hand in the frame is left alone and is read with them.
          */
          notation { drawnScore() }
          println("${notation.mine.size} marks drawn")
  - create:
      box: ds_read
      name: read
      frame: { x: 20.0, y: 500.0, w: 190.0, h: 60.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // Eight beats across, MIDI 84 at the top down to 48 at the bottom: every mark as an event.
          val score = notation.space("score", x = 0.0..8.0, y = 84.0..48.0)
          println(
              score.events.joinToString("\n") { e ->
                  "%s: beat %.3f to %.3f, MIDI %.2f to %.2f"
                      .format(e.mark.label ?: e.mark.kind.name.lowercase(), e.start, e.end, e.value, e.endValue)
              },
          )
  - create:
      box: ds_play
      name: play
      frame: { x: 300.0, y: 500.0, w: 190.0, h: 60.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // What each mark means as music is decided here, and you can change it.
          val score = notation.space("score", x = 0.0..8.0, y = 84.0..48.0) // eight beats; MIDI 84 at the top
          val glideStep = 0.125 // how finely a moving stroke is read

          val notes = mutableListOf<TimedNote>()
          for (e in score.events) {
              val kind = e.mark.kind
              if (kind == MarkType.TEXT || kind == MarkType.FRAME || kind == MarkType.ARROW) continue // labels, not notes
              if (e.end <= e.start) continue // no width, no time
              val moving = (kind == MarkType.STROKE || kind == MarkType.LINE) && kotlin.math.abs(e.endValue - e.value) > 0.5
              if (!moving) { // a rectangle, or a level line: one note
                  notes += TimedNote(e.start, e.end, e.value)
                  continue
              }
              var t = e.start // a glissando: cut it every glideStep
              while (t < e.end - 1e-9) {
                  val hit = score.vertical(t).firstOrNull { it.mark.id == e.mark.id && !it.isSpan }
                  if (hit != null) notes += TimedNote(t, minOf(t + glideStep, e.end), hit.value, hit.pressure ?: 1.0)
                  t += glideStep
              }
          }

          val voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.TRIANGLE, decay = 0.004, sustain = 0.4)
          showPatRollOf(
              "read" to patTimed(notes, beats = 8.0),
              title = "the score, read",
              subtitle = "${notes.size} notes",
              cycles = 1,
              pitched = true,
              channel = "roll",
          )
          showPatAudio(patTimed(notes, beats = 8.0), cycles = 2, cps = 0.25, voice = voice, channel = "audio")
  - create:
      box: ds_pentatonic
      name: pentatonic
      frame: { x: 580.0, y: 500.0, w: 190.0, h: 60.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // The same drawing read another way: every note snapped to C minor pentatonic.
          val notes = DrawnScoreDocs.interpret(notation.space("score", x = 0.0..8.0, y = 84.0..48.0)) // the loop in `play`

          val minorPentatonic = setOf(0, 3, 5, 7, 10) // C Eb F G Bb
          val inScale = (24..108).filter { it % 12 in minorPentatonic }
          val snap = { midi: Double -> inScale.minBy { kotlin.math.abs(it - midi) }.toDouble() }
          val tuned = mutableListOf<TimedNote>()
          for (n in notes.map { it.copy(note = snap(it.note)) }) {
              val last = tuned.lastOrNull()
              if (last != null && last.note == n.note && last.end == n.start)
                  tuned[tuned.size - 1] = last.copy(end = n.end) // same pitch: hold it
              else tuned += n
          }

          val voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.TRIANGLE, decay = 0.004, sustain = 0.4)
          showPatRollOf(
              "read" to patTimed(notes, beats = 8.0),
              "C minor pentatonic" to patTimed(tuned, beats = 8.0),
              title = "one drawing, two readings",
              cycles = 1,
              pitched = true,
              channel = "roll",
          )
          showPatAudio(patTimed(tuned, beats = 8.0), cycles = 2, cps = 0.25, voice = voice, channel = "audio")
  - create:
      box: ds_listen
      name: listen back
      frame: { x: 860.0, y: 500.0, w: 190.0, h: 60.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // Play both readings again, then take the sound apart: an onset per strike, a pitch per note.
          val notes = DrawnScoreDocs.interpret(notation.space("score", x = 0.0..8.0, y = 84.0..48.0))
          val tuned = DrawnScoreDocs.pentatonic(notes)
          val voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.TRIANGLE, decay = 0.004, sustain = 0.4)
          val heard = listOf(notes, tuned).map {
              DrawnScoreDocs.listen(patRenderStereo(patTimed(it, beats = 8.0), cycles = 2, cps = 0.25, voice = voice), it)
          }
          val trace = heard[0].trace()
          showSignals(
              "drawn" to trace.map { it.third },
              "heard" to trace.map { it.second },
              x = trace.map { it.first },
              title = "pitch: drawn and heard",
              xTitle = "seconds",
              yTitle = "MIDI",
          )
          println(heard.joinToString("\n") { it.describe() })
  - execute:
      box: ds_score
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: ds_read
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: ds_play
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: ds_pentatonic
      property: code
  - execute:
      box: ds_listen
      property: code

before:
name: dynamic_graph_systems_examples
description: >
  The dynamic-graph family (public/docs/dynamic_graph_systems_examples.md) as six independent
  pure-CPU boxes: point clouds that move while the graph joining them is continually reinforced and
  forgotten. Four of them measure and print, two of them animate.
  The measuring boxes print the numbers the page quotes and the tests assert -- all six
  DynamicGraphSystems over one cloud, told apart by the exact fraction of their edges that close a
  triangle (0 % for flowline advection, 100 % for the tangent fan and for alpha-event collapse); both
  decay laws against their closed forms at 1, 4 and 120 steps plus ttl expiring an edge that is still
  at its ceiling; hysteresis against a control arm with rExit == rEnter, which creates 1.80x as many
  edges and loses 7.9x as many; and the weight threshold recovering exactly the four co-moving groups
  ([240, 22, 22, 22]) out of a graph that has only ever seen positions and a clock.
  The two animating boxes are Box.animateEvolution schedules and must be LAUNCHED, not run -- a
  Frames that is only built never runs, so executing one of them is a compile check and nothing more.
  The breathing box is the clearest thing here: the cloud never moves, so every edge that appears is
  the anisotropic metric turning, and the right-hand panel is the identical system with its clock
  pinned at zero. The morphogenesis box grows a 64-point ring into a branching filament against the
  same pipeline with tip growth removed. None of the six opens a Window or a Renderer.
  The three graph figures are VECTOR -- dynamicGraphFLines into showPlaneGrid, so one FLine per
  edge with weight driving colour and thickness -- and only the two clips use the dynamicGraphPanel
  raster, because animateEvolution's panels are typed on Img. Reach for dynamicGraphFLines when you
  are writing a new still here.
operations:
  - create:
      box: dgs_six_systems
      name: "1 — six ways to propose an edge"
      frame:
        x: 60.0
        y: 60.0
        w: 320.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          Six DynamicGraphSystems, one cloud, one clock, one reinforcement budget. The only thing
          that differs between panels is what the system thinks an edge means. Brightness is
          weight / 4.0 -- the shared ceiling -- so it is a FIXED scale and a dim panel is a system
          whose weights genuinely stayed low.
          */
          val cloud =
              List(220) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val r = 0.5 * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / 220.0)
                  Vec3((r * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (r * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          val window = dynamicGraphWindow(cloud, padFraction = 0.06)
          val ceiling = 4.0

          fun build(system: DynamicGraphSystem): Pair<DynamicPointState, DynamicEdgeList> {
              val state = DynamicPointState(cloud.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList())
              val edges = DynamicEdgeList(state.pointCount)
              val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.06)
              repeat(20) { stepDynamicGraph(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system) }
              return state to edges
          }

          val systems = listOf<Pair<String, DynamicGraphSystem>>(
              "kNN k=5" to
                  Vec3BreathingAnisotropicKnnSystem(
                      k = 5,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      mutualOnly = true,
                      queryRadius = 0.12,
                  ),
              "flowline" to
                  Vec3FlowlineAdvectionGraphSystem(
                      influenceRadius = 0.10,
                      stepLength = 0.08,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                  ),
              "tangent fan" to
                  Vec3LocalTangentTriangulationSystem(
                      neighborhoodK = 6,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      maxNeighborRadius = 0.10,
                  ),
              "hysteresis" to
                  Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                      rEnter = 0.055,
                      rExit = 0.075,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                  ),
              "routing, 1 arc" to
                  Vec3SignalRoutingGraphSystem(
                      neighborhoodK = 6,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 1.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      routeCount = 1,
                      maxNeighborRadius = 0.10,
                  ),
              "alpha-event" to
                  Vec3AlphaEventHypergraphCollapseSystem(
                      neighborhoodK = 6,
                      alphaRadius = 0.075,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforcePerUnitArea = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      maxNeighborRadius = 0.09,
                      minArea = 1e-4,
                  ),
          )

          // "What fraction of edges close a triangle" is the one exact structural fact separating the
          // six: it is 0 % for a functional map and 100 % for anything that builds faces.
          val panels = systems.map { (name, system) ->
              val (state, edges) = build(system)
              val adjacency = Array(state.pointCount) { HashSet<Int>() }
              for (e in edges.values()) {
                  adjacency[e.i].add(e.j)
                  adjacency[e.j].add(e.i)
              }
              val closed =
                  edges.values().count { e ->
                      adjacency[e.i].any { it != e.j && adjacency[e.j].contains(it) }
                  }
              val fraction = if (edges.values().isEmpty()) 0.0 else closed.toDouble() / edges.values().size
              val wmax = edges.values().maxOfOrNull { it.weight } ?: 0.0
              println(
                  "%-16s %4d edges  %5.1f%% in a triangle  mean degree %.2f  wmax %.4f (%.1f%% of ceiling)"
                      .format(
                          name,
                          edges.values().size,
                          100.0 * fraction,
                          2.0 * edges.values().size / state.pointCount,
                          wmax,
                          100.0 * wmax / ceiling,
                      ),
              )
              // dynamicGraphFLines, not dynamicGraphPanel: a still figure is VECTOR here -- one FLine
              // per edge, weight driving colour AND thickness, through showPlaneGrid -> drawToSVG.
              "%s: %de %d%%tri".format(name, edges.values().size, Math.round(100.0 * fraction)) to
                  dynamicGraphFLines(state.points, edges.values(), maxWeight = ceiling, colormap = "magma")
          }

          // One shared window, so nothing but the topology differs between the six panels.
          showPlaneGrid(
              *panels.toTypedArray(),
              columns = 3,
              cellWidth = 400,
              cellHeight = 400,
              window = dynamicGraphPlaneWindow(window),
          )
  - create:
      box: dgs_decay
      name: "2 — reinforcement and forgetting"
      frame:
        x: 530.0
        y: 60.0
        w: 330.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          // One edge under each decay law, starting at weight 1, stepped at 60 frames a second for four seconds.
          val exponential = DynamicEdgeList(2)
          val linear = DynamicEdgeList(2)
          exponential.reinforce(0, 1, 1.0, ttl = 1000f, maxWeight = 1.0)
          linear.reinforce(0, 1, 1.0, ttl = 1000f, maxWeight = 1.0)

          val expo = mutableListOf<Double>()
          val lin = mutableListOf<Double>()
          repeat(240) {
              expo += exponential.get(0, 1)?.weight ?: 0.0
              lin += linear.get(0, 1)?.weight ?: 0.0
              exponential.decayExponential(1f / 60f, 0.35)
              linear.decayLinear(1f / 60f, 0.35)
          }

          showSignals(
              "exponential, λ = 0.35" to expo,
              "linear, 0.35 / s" to lin,
              x = List(240) { it / 60.0 },
          )
  - create:
      box: dgs_hysteresis
      name: "3 — hysteresis, against a memoryless control"
      frame:
        x: 1000.0
        y: 60.0
        w: 400.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          // A 200-point disc, each point wobbling by up to 0.012 a frame: about a fifth of rEnter, enough to
          // cross the threshold without rearranging the neighbourhood.
          val n = 200
          val base =
              List(n) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val r = 0.45 * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / n)
                  Vec3((r * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (r * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          // Both panels share one window, computed from the cloud at rest, so they are drawn at the same scale.
          val window = dynamicGraphWindow(base, padFraction = 0.06)

          class Flicker(val appeared: Int, val vanished: Int, val standing: Int, val lines: List<FLine>)

          // Run the cloud for 150 frames and count the edges created and lost along the way.
          fun flicker(rExit: Double): Flicker {
              val state = DynamicPointState(base.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList())
              val edges = DynamicEdgeList(n)
              val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.06)
              val system = Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                  rEnter = 0.055,
                  rExit = rExit,
                  ttl = 0.35f,
                  reinforce = 3.0,
                  maxWeight = 3.0,
              )
              var appeared = 0
              var vanished = 0
              var present = HashSet<Pair<Int, Int>>()
              repeat(150) { frame ->
                  for (i in 0 until n) {
                      val phase = 0.31 * i + 0.16 * frame
                      state.points[i] =
                          Vec3(base[i])
                              .add(
                                  vec(0.012 * Math.cos(phase), 0.012 * Math.sin(1.7 * phase), 0.0),
                              )
                  }
                  stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.9)
                  val now = edges.values().map { it.i to it.j }.toHashSet()
                  appeared += (now - present).size
                  vanished += (present - now).size
                  present = now
              }
              return Flicker(
                  appeared,
                  vanished,
                  present.size,
                  dynamicGraphFLines(state.points, edges.values(), maxWeight = 3.0, colormap = "magma"),
              )
          }

          // rExit == rEnter switches hysteresis off.
          val on = flicker(rExit = 0.075)
          val off = flicker(rExit = 0.055)
          println("hysteresis on:  ${on.appeared} edges created, ${on.vanished} lost, ${on.standing} standing after 150 frames")
          println(
              "hysteresis off: ${off.appeared} edges created, ${off.vanished} lost, ${off.standing} standing after 150 frames",
          )

          showPlaneGrid(
              "rExit 0.075: ${on.appeared} in, ${on.vanished} out" to on.lines,
              "rExit = rEnter: ${off.appeared} in, ${off.vanished} out" to off.lines,
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 460,
              cellHeight = 460,
              window = dynamicGraphPlaneWindow(window),
          )

          // Two points walked apart from 0.05 to 0.13: past rEnter (0.10), inside rExit (0.16).
          fun walk(rExit: Double): Pair<Boolean, Boolean> {
              val state = DynamicPointState(mutableListOf(Vec3(0f, 0f, 0f), Vec3(0.05f, 0f, 0f)))
              val edges = DynamicEdgeList(2)
              val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.2)
              val system = Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                  rEnter = 0.10,
                  rExit = rExit,
                  ttl = 0.2f,
                  reinforce = 4.0,
                  maxWeight = 8.0,
              )
              repeat(30) { stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.2) }
              val formedWhileClose = edges.get(0, 1) != null
              state.points[1] = Vec3(0.13f, 0f, 0f)
              repeat(60) { stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.2) }
              return formedWhileClose to (edges.get(0, 1) != null)
          }

          for (rExit in listOf(0.16, 0.10)) {
              val (formed, survives) = walk(rExit)
              println("rExit $rExit: formed at d=0.05 = $formed, survives d=0.13 = $survives")
          }
  - create:
      box: dgs_threshold
      name: "4 — the weight threshold recovers the co-moving groups"
      frame:
        x: 60.0
        y: 300.0
        w: 470.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          A static 240-point background mesh with three rigid 22-point clusters crossing it.
          Cluster-internal pairs are adjacent for the whole four seconds; cluster-to-background
          pairs only in passing. The minWeight cut has to tell those apart using nothing but
          accumulated weight -- and it recovers the groups exactly.
          */
          fun disc(n: Int, r: Double) =
              List(n) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val rad = r * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / n)
                  Vec3((rad * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (rad * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }

          val nBg = 240
          val perCluster = 22
          val n = nBg + 3 * perCluster
          val background = disc(nBg, 0.50)
          val blobs = List(3) { disc(perCluster, 0.070) }
          val starts = listOf(Vec3(-0.44f, -0.20f, 0f), Vec3(-0.30f, 0.40f, 0f), Vec3(0.34f, -0.44f, 0f))
          val velocities = listOf(Vec3(0.20f, 0.07f, 0f), Vec3(0.16f, -0.19f, 0f), Vec3(-0.12f, 0.20f, 0f))
          // Used ONLY to check the answer, never to build the graph.
          val group = IntArray(n) { if (it < nBg) -1 else (it - nBg) / perCluster }

          val points = MutableList(n) { Vec3(0f, 0f, 0f) }
          for (i in 0 until nBg) points[i] = Vec3(background[i])
          val state = DynamicPointState(points)
          val edges = DynamicEdgeList(n)
          val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.055)
          val ceiling = 3.0
          val system = Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
              rEnter = 0.062,
              rExit = 0.075,
              ttl = 0.4f,
              reinforce = 2.5,
              maxWeight = ceiling,
          )

          repeat(240) { f ->
              val t = f / 60.0
              for (c in 0 until 3) {
                  val centre = Vec3(starts[c]).add(Vec3(velocities[c]).mul(t.toFloat()))
                  for (k in 0 until perCluster) {
                      state.points[nBg + c * perCluster + k] = Vec3(blobs[c][k]).add(centre)
                  }
              }
              stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.30)
          }
          println(dynamicGraphSummary(state, edges))

          fun componentSizes(graph: PointGraph): List<Int> {
              val parent = IntArray(graph.pointCount) { it }
              fun find(a: Int): Int {
                  var x = a
                  while (parent[x] != x) {
                      parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
                      x = parent[x]
                  }
                  return x
              }
              for (e in graph.edges) {
                  val ra = find(e.i)
                  val rb = find(e.j)
                  if (ra != rb) parent[ra] = rb
              }
              val sizes = HashMap<Int, Int>()
              for (v in 0 until graph.pointCount) sizes.merge(find(v), 1) { a, b -> a + b }
              return sizes.values.sortedDescending()
          }

          // Pinned rather than fitted: the clusters are somewhere else at t = 0 and at t = 4 s, so a
          // window derived from the final frame would frame a different picture from the run's.
          val window = doubleArrayOf(-0.60, -0.60, 0.60, 0.60)
          println("points outside that window: ${dynamicGraphOutsideWindow(state.points, window)}")
          val panels =
              listOf(0.0, 0.5, 1.2, 2.0).map { cut ->
                  val graph = edges.toPointGraph(minWeight = cut)
                  val groups = componentSizes(graph).filter { it > 1 }
                  val cross = graph.edges.count { group[it.i] != group[it.j] }
                  println(
                      "minWeight %.1f -> %4d edges, %3d crossing a group boundary, components > 1: %s"
                          .format(
                              cut,
                              graph.edges.size,
                              cross,
                              groups,
                          ),
                  )
                  val kept = edges.values().filter { it.weight > cut }
                  "w>%.1f  %de  %d groups".format(cut, graph.edges.size, groups.size) to
                      dynamicGraphFLines(state.points, kept, maxWeight = ceiling, colormap = "magma")
              }
          showPlaneGrid(
              *panels.toTypedArray(),
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 430,
              cellHeight = 430,
              window = dynamicGraphPlaneWindow(window),
          )
  - create:
      box: dgs_breathing
      name: "5 — LAUNCH ME: the graph rewiring while nothing moves"
      frame:
        x: 530.0
        y: 300.0
        w: 460.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          LAUNCH this box (animate/loop), do not just run it: animateEvolution returns a Frames,
          and a Frames that is only built never runs.

          The cloud NEVER MOVES. Every edge that appears or disappears is the anisotropic metric
          breathing -- an axis that rotates with the clock and a stretch along it between 0.25 and
          2.0. The right-hand panel is the control: same k, same cloud, same code path, clock
          pinned at zero, so it holds exactly 590 edges for all 420 steps.
          */
          val n = 260
          val cloud =
              List(n) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val r = 0.5 * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / n)
                  Vec3((r * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (r * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          val window = dynamicGraphWindow(cloud, padFraction = 0.06)
          val ceiling = 1.2

          class Breath(
              val warped: DynamicPointState,
              val plain: DynamicPointState,
              val warpedEdges: DynamicEdgeList,
              val plainEdges: DynamicEdgeList,
              val hash: Vec3SpatialHash,
          )

          val warpedSystem = Vec3BreathingAnisotropicKnnSystem(
              k = 5,
              ttl = 0.25f,
              reinforce = 6.0,
              maxWeight = ceiling,
              mutualOnly = true,
              queryRadius = 0.13,
          )
          val plainSystem = Vec3BreathingAnisotropicKnnSystem(
              k = 5,
              ttl = 0.25f,
              reinforce = 6.0,
              maxWeight = ceiling,
              mutualOnly = true,
              queryRadius = 0.13,
          )

          val seed = Breath(
              DynamicPointState(cloud.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList()),
              DynamicPointState(cloud.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList()),
              DynamicEdgeList(n),
              DynamicEdgeList(n),
              Vec3SpatialHash(0.065),
          )

          animateEvolution(
              seed,
              totalSteps = 420,
              seconds = 8.0,
              columns = 2,
              cellSide = 460,
              framesTarget = 160,
              step = { s ->
                  stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(
                      1f / 60f,
                      s.warped,
                      s.warpedEdges,
                      s.hash,
                      warpedSystem,
                      2.5,
                  )
                  // The system advances state.time itself, so pinning it either side of the call is
                  // what "the same code with the time-dependence removed" means.
                  s.plain.time = 0f
                  stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(
                      1f / 60f,
                      s.plain,
                      s.plainEdges,
                      s.hash,
                      plainSystem,
                      2.5,
                  )
                  s.plain.time = 0f
                  s
              },
              panels = { s, step ->
                  listOf(
                      "breathing, t=%.2fs, %d edges".format(s.warped.time, s.warpedEdges.values().size) to
                          dynamicGraphPanel(s.warped.points, s.warpedEdges.values(), window, 460, 460, ceiling, "magma"),
                      "frozen, step %d, %d edges".format(step, s.plainEdges.values().size) to
                          dynamicGraphPanel(s.plain.points, s.plainEdges.values(), window, 460, 460, ceiling, "magma"),
                  )
              },
          )
  - create:
      box: dgs_morphogenesis
      name: "6 — LAUNCH ME: morphogenesis, and its tip-growth-off twin"
      frame:
        x: 1000.0
        y: 300.0
        w: 480.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          LAUNCH this box, do not just run it.

          The full pipeline: diffuse a resource along the edges and climb its gradient, relax the
          springs, grow tips where the incident edges pull coherently, merge what has collided,
          smooth, jitter. The right-hand panel is the same pipeline with ONE stage removed -- tip
          growth -- so the difference between the panels is that stage and nothing else.
          */
          val seedRing =
              List(64) { i ->
                  val a = 2.0 * Math.PI * i / 64
                  Vec3((0.42 * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (0.42 * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          // Sized for where the structure ENDS UP. Re-fitting per frame would make growth invisible.
          val window = doubleArrayOf(-0.95, -0.95, 0.95, 0.95)
          val ceiling = 3.0

          class Morph(
              val state: DynamicPointState,
              val kinetics: DynamicPointKinetics,
              val edges: DynamicEdgeList,
              val hash: Vec3SpatialHash,
              val pipeline: DynamicProcessPipeline,
              val system: DynamicGraphSystem,
          )

          fun morph(grow: Boolean): Morph {
              val state = DynamicPointState(seedRing.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList())
              val kinetics = DynamicPointKinetics(mutableListOf(), mutableListOf(), mutableListOf())
              kinetics.ensureSize(state.pointCount)
              // Seed the resource on a quarter of the ring, so chemotaxis has a gradient to climb.
              for (i in 0 until 16) kinetics.resource[i] = 6.0
              val stages = mutableListOf<DynamicPointProcess>(
                  SignalDiffusionAndChemotaxisProcess(diffusionRate = 0.5, chemoGain = 0.35, maxSpeed = 0.30),
                  // rest = restLengthTimesWeight / weight: 0.075 is a rest length of 0.05 at a typical
                  // weight of 1.5.
                  SpringMotionProcess(springK = 1.2, damping = 3.0, restLengthTimesWeight = 0.075, maxSpeed = 0.30),
              )
              if (grow)
                  stages +=
                      DirectedTipGrowthProcess(
                          coherenceThreshold = 1.6,
                          spawnDistance = 0.035,
                          localDensityRadius = 0.05,
                          localDensityMax = 6,
                          childEdgeWeight = 1.5,
                          childEdgeTtl = 1.5f,
                          maxWeight = ceiling,
                          maxPointCount = 900,
                      )
              stages += MergeClosePointsProcess(mergeDistance = 0.012, minCombinedWeight = 2.0)
              stages += RelaxToMidpointProcess(gain = 1.5)
              stages += JitterProcess(amplitude = 0.04)
              return Morph(
                  state,
                  kinetics,
                  DynamicEdgeList(state.pointCount),
                  Vec3SpatialHash(0.05),
                  DynamicProcessPipeline(stages),
                  Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                      rEnter = 0.05,
                      rExit = 0.07,
                      ttl = 0.8f,
                      reinforce = 3.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                  ),
              )
          }

          animateEvolution(
              morph(grow = true) to morph(grow = false),
              totalSteps = 560,
              seconds = 10.0,
              columns = 2,
              cellSide = 490,
              framesTarget = 200,
              // Geometric: the 900-point cap is reached at step 79, so a linear schedule would spend
              // seven eighths of the clip on the aftermath. ramp = 25 puts the mid-point at step 93.
              ramp = 25.0,
              step = { (grown, flat) ->
                  for (m in listOf(grown, flat)) {
                      stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(
                          1f / 60f,
                          m.state,
                          m.edges,
                          m.hash,
                          m.system,
                          0.6,
                      )
                      m.pipeline.step(1f / 60f, m.state, m.kinetics, m.edges, m.hash)
                  }
                  grown to flat
              },
              panels = { (grown, flat), step ->
                  listOf(
                      "grow ON  s%d  %dpts %de"
                          .format(
                              step,
                              grown.state.pointCount,
                              grown.edges.values().size,
                          ) to dynamicGraphPanel(grown.state.points, grown.edges.values(), window, 490, 490, ceiling, "magma"),
                      "grow OFF  s%d  %dpts %de"
                          .format(
                              step,
                              flat.state.pointCount,
                              flat.edges.values().size,
                          ) to dynamicGraphPanel(flat.state.points, flat.edges.values(), window, 490, 490, ceiling, "magma"),
                  )
              },
          )
  # Bare `execute` ops run each box's stored `code`. The four measuring boxes print the numbers this
  # family's page quotes and its tests assert. The two animating boxes are deliberately NOT executed
  # here: animateEvolution returns a Frames, which only runs when the box is launched, so executing
  # one would be a compile check dressed up as a demonstration. Launch them yourself.
  - execute:
      box: dgs_six_systems
  - execute:
      box: dgs_decay
  - execute:
      box: dgs_hysteresis
  - execute:
      box: dgs_threshold
after:
name: dynamic_graph_systems_examples
description: >

  pure-CPU boxes: point clouds that move while the graph joining them is continually reinforced and

  The measuring boxes print the numbers the page quotes and the tests assert -- all six
  DynamicGraphSystems over one cloud, told apart by the exact fraction of their edges that close a

  decay laws against their closed forms at 1, 4 and 120 steps plus ttl expiring an edge that is still
  at its ceiling; hysteresis against a control arm with rExit == rEnter, which creates 1.80x as many
  edges and loses 7.9x as many; and the weight threshold recovering exactly the four co-moving groups
  ([240, 22, 22, 22]) out of a graph that has only ever seen positions and a clock.
  The two animating boxes are Box.animateEvolution schedules and must be LAUNCHED, not run -- a
  Frames that is only built never runs, so executing one of them is a compile check and nothing more.
  The breathing box is the clearest thing here: the cloud never moves, so every edge that appears is
  the anisotropic metric turning, and the right-hand panel is the identical system with its clock
  pinned at zero. The morphogenesis box grows a 64-point ring into a branching filament against the
  same pipeline with tip growth removed. None of the six opens a Window or a Renderer.
  The three graph figures are VECTOR -- dynamicGraphFLines into showPlaneGrid, so one FLine per
  edge with weight driving colour and thickness -- and only the two clips use the dynamicGraphPanel
  raster, because animateEvolution's panels are typed on Img. Reach for dynamicGraphFLines when you

operations:

        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          Six DynamicGraphSystems, one cloud, one clock, one reinforcement budget. The only thing
          that differs between panels is what the system thinks an edge means. Brightness is
          weight / 4.0 -- the shared ceiling -- so it is a FIXED scale and a dim panel is a system
          whose weights genuinely stayed low.
          */
          val cloud =
              List(220) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val r = 0.5 * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / 220.0)
                  Vec3((r * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (r * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          val window = dynamicGraphWindow(cloud, padFraction = 0.06)
          val ceiling = 4.0

          fun build(system: DynamicGraphSystem): Pair<DynamicPointState, DynamicEdgeList> {
              val state = DynamicPointState(cloud.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList())
              val edges = DynamicEdgeList(state.pointCount)
              val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.06)
              repeat(20) { stepDynamicGraph(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system) }
              return state to edges
          }

          val systems = listOf<Pair<String, DynamicGraphSystem>>(
              "kNN k=5" to
                  Vec3BreathingAnisotropicKnnSystem(
                      k = 5,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      mutualOnly = true,
                      queryRadius = 0.12,
                  ),
              "flowline" to
                  Vec3FlowlineAdvectionGraphSystem(
                      influenceRadius = 0.10,
                      stepLength = 0.08,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                  ),
              "tangent fan" to
                  Vec3LocalTangentTriangulationSystem(
                      neighborhoodK = 6,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      maxNeighborRadius = 0.10,
                  ),
              "hysteresis" to
                  Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                      rEnter = 0.055,
                      rExit = 0.075,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                  ),
              "routing, 1 arc" to
                  Vec3SignalRoutingGraphSystem(
                      neighborhoodK = 6,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforce = 1.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      routeCount = 1,
                      maxNeighborRadius = 0.10,
                  ),
              "alpha-event" to
                  Vec3AlphaEventHypergraphCollapseSystem(
                      neighborhoodK = 6,
                      alphaRadius = 0.075,
                      ttl = 10f,
                      reinforcePerUnitArea = 4.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                      maxNeighborRadius = 0.09,
                      minArea = 1e-4,
                  ),
          )

          // "What fraction of edges close a triangle" is the one exact structural fact separating the
          // six: it is 0 % for a functional map and 100 % for anything that builds faces.
          val panels = systems.map { (name, system) ->
              val (state, edges) = build(system)
              val adjacency = Array(state.pointCount) { HashSet<Int>() }
              for (e in edges.values()) {
                  adjacency[e.i].add(e.j)
                  adjacency[e.j].add(e.i)
              }
              val closed =
                  edges.values().count { e ->
                      adjacency[e.i].any { it != e.j && adjacency[e.j].contains(it) }
                  }
              val fraction = if (edges.values().isEmpty()) 0.0 else closed.toDouble() / edges.values().size
              val wmax = edges.values().maxOfOrNull { it.weight } ?: 0.0
              println(
                  "%-16s %4d edges  %5.1f%% in a triangle  mean degree %.2f  wmax %.4f (%.1f%% of ceiling)"
                      .format(
                          name,
                          edges.values().size,
                          100.0 * fraction,
                          2.0 * edges.values().size / state.pointCount,
                          wmax,
                          100.0 * wmax / ceiling,
                      ),
              )
              // dynamicGraphFLines, not dynamicGraphPanel: a still figure is VECTOR here -- one FLine
              // per edge, weight driving colour AND thickness, through showPlaneGrid -> drawToSVG.
              "%s: %de %d%%tri".format(name, edges.values().size, Math.round(100.0 * fraction)) to
                  dynamicGraphFLines(state.points, edges.values(), maxWeight = ceiling, colormap = "magma")
          }

          // One shared window, so nothing but the topology differs between the six panels.
          showPlaneGrid(
              *panels.toTypedArray(),
              columns = 3,
              cellWidth = 400,
              cellHeight = 400,
              window = dynamicGraphPlaneWindow(window),
          )
  - create:
      box: dgs_decay
      name: "2 — reinforcement and forgetting"
      frame:
        x: 530.0
        y: 60.0
        w: 330.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          // One edge under each decay law, starting at weight 1, stepped at 60 frames a second for four seconds.
          val exponential = DynamicEdgeList(2)
          val linear = DynamicEdgeList(2)
          exponential.reinforce(0, 1, 1.0, ttl = 1000f, maxWeight = 1.0)
          linear.reinforce(0, 1, 1.0, ttl = 1000f, maxWeight = 1.0)

          val expo = mutableListOf<Double>()
          val lin = mutableListOf<Double>()
          repeat(240) {
              expo += exponential.get(0, 1)?.weight ?: 0.0
              lin += linear.get(0, 1)?.weight ?: 0.0
              exponential.decayExponential(1f / 60f, 0.35)
              linear.decayLinear(1f / 60f, 0.35)
          }

          showSignals(
              "exponential, λ = 0.35" to expo,

  - create:
      box: dgs_hysteresis
      name: "3 — hysteresis, against a memoryless control"
      frame:
        x: 1000.0
        y: 60.0
        w: 400.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          // A 200-point disc, each point wobbling by up to 0.012 a frame: about a fifth of rEnter, enough to
          // cross the threshold without rearranging the neighbourhood.
          val n = 200
          val base =
              List(n) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val r = 0.45 * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / n)
                  Vec3((r * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (r * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          // Both panels share one window, computed from the cloud at rest, so they are drawn at the same scale.
          val window = dynamicGraphWindow(base, padFraction = 0.06)

          class Flicker(val appeared: Int, val vanished: Int, val standing: Int, val lines: List<FLine>)

          // Run the cloud for 150 frames and count the edges created and lost along the way.
          fun flicker(rExit: Double): Flicker {
              val state = DynamicPointState(base.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList())
              val edges = DynamicEdgeList(n)
              val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.06)
              val system = Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                  rEnter = 0.055,
                  rExit = rExit,
                  ttl = 0.35f,
                  reinforce = 3.0,
                  maxWeight = 3.0,
              )
              var appeared = 0
              var vanished = 0
              var present = HashSet<Pair<Int, Int>>()
              repeat(150) { frame ->
                  for (i in 0 until n) {
                      val phase = 0.31 * i + 0.16 * frame
                      state.points[i] =
                          Vec3(base[i])
                              .add(
                                  vec(0.012 * Math.cos(phase), 0.012 * Math.sin(1.7 * phase), 0.0),
                              )
                  }
                  stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.9)
                  val now = edges.values().map { it.i to it.j }.toHashSet()
                  appeared += (now - present).size
                  vanished += (present - now).size
                  present = now
              }
              return Flicker(
                  appeared,
                  vanished,
                  present.size,
                  dynamicGraphFLines(state.points, edges.values(), maxWeight = 3.0, colormap = "magma"),
              )
          }

          // rExit == rEnter switches hysteresis off.
          val on = flicker(rExit = 0.075)
          val off = flicker(rExit = 0.055)
          println("hysteresis on:  ${on.appeared} edges created, ${on.vanished} lost, ${on.standing} standing after 150 frames")
          println(
              "hysteresis off: ${off.appeared} edges created, ${off.vanished} lost, ${off.standing} standing after 150 frames",
          )

          showPlaneGrid(
              "rExit 0.075: ${on.appeared} in, ${on.vanished} out" to on.lines,
              "rExit = rEnter: ${off.appeared} in, ${off.vanished} out" to off.lines,
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 460,
              cellHeight = 460,
              window = dynamicGraphPlaneWindow(window),
          )

          // Two points walked apart from 0.05 to 0.13: past rEnter (0.10), inside rExit (0.16).
          fun walk(rExit: Double): Pair<Boolean, Boolean> {
              val state = DynamicPointState(mutableListOf(Vec3(0f, 0f, 0f), Vec3(0.05f, 0f, 0f)))
              val edges = DynamicEdgeList(2)
              val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.2)
              val system = Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                  rEnter = 0.10,
                  rExit = rExit,
                  ttl = 0.2f,
                  reinforce = 4.0,
                  maxWeight = 8.0,
              )
              repeat(30) { stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.2) }
              val formedWhileClose = edges.get(0, 1) != null
              state.points[1] = Vec3(0.13f, 0f, 0f)
              repeat(60) { stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.2) }
              return formedWhileClose to (edges.get(0, 1) != null)
          }

          for (rExit in [0.16, 0.10]) {
              val (formed, survives) = walk(rExit)
              println("rExit $rExit: formed at d=0.05 = $formed, survives d=0.13 = $survives")
          }
  - create:
      box: dgs_threshold
      name: "4 — the weight threshold recovers the co-moving groups"
      frame:
        x: 60.0
        y: 300.0
        w: 470.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          A static 240-point background mesh with three rigid 22-point clusters crossing it.
          Cluster-internal pairs are adjacent for the whole four seconds; cluster-to-background
          pairs only in passing. The minWeight cut has to tell those apart using nothing but
          accumulated weight -- and it recovers the groups exactly.
          */
          fun disc(n: Int, r: Double) =
              List(n) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val rad = r * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / n)
                  Vec3((rad * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (rad * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }

          val nBg = 240
          val perCluster = 22
          val n = nBg + 3 * perCluster
          val background = disc(nBg, 0.50)
          val blobs = List(3) { disc(perCluster, 0.070) }
          val starts = [Vec3(-0.44f, -0.20f, 0f), Vec3(-0.30f, 0.40f, 0f), Vec3(0.34f, -0.44f, 0f)]
          val velocities = [Vec3(0.20f, 0.07f, 0f), Vec3(0.16f, -0.19f, 0f), Vec3(-0.12f, 0.20f, 0f)]
          // Used ONLY to check the answer, never to build the graph.
          val group = IntArray(n) { if (it < nBg) -1 else (it - nBg) / perCluster }

          val points = MutableList(n) { Vec3(0f, 0f, 0f) }
          for (i in 0 until nBg) points[i] = Vec3(background[i])
          val state = DynamicPointState(points)
          val edges = DynamicEdgeList(n)
          val hash = Vec3SpatialHash(0.055)
          val ceiling = 3.0
          val system = Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
              rEnter = 0.062,
              rExit = 0.075,
              ttl = 0.4f,
              reinforce = 2.5,
              maxWeight = ceiling,
          )

          repeat(240) { f ->
              val t = f / 60.0
              for (c in 0 until 3) {
                  val centre = Vec3(starts[c]).add(Vec3(velocities[c]).mul(t.toFloat()))
                  for (k in 0 until perCluster) {
                      state.points[nBg + c * perCluster + k] = Vec3(blobs[c][k]).add(centre)
                  }
              }
              stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(1f / 60f, state, edges, hash, system, 0.30)
          }
          println(dynamicGraphSummary(state, edges))

          fun componentSizes(graph: PointGraph): List<Int> {
              val parent = IntArray(graph.pointCount) { it }
              fun find(a: Int): Int {
                  var x = a
                  while (parent[x] != x) {
                      parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
                      x = parent[x]
                  }
                  return x
              }
              for (e in graph.edges) {
                  val ra = find(e.i)
                  val rb = find(e.j)
                  if (ra != rb) parent[ra] = rb
              }
              val sizes = HashMap<Int, Int>()
              for (v in 0 until graph.pointCount) sizes.merge(find(v), 1) { a, b -> a + b }
              return sizes.values.sortedDescending()
          }

          // Pinned rather than fitted: the clusters are somewhere else at t = 0 and at t = 4 s, so a
          // window derived from the final frame would frame a different picture from the run's.
          val window = doubleArrayOf(-0.60, -0.60, 0.60, 0.60)
          println("points outside that window: ${dynamicGraphOutsideWindow(state.points, window)}")
          val panels =
              [0.0, 0.5, 1.2, 2.0].map { cut ->
                  val graph = edges.toPointGraph(minWeight = cut)
                  val groups = componentSizes(graph).filter { it > 1 }
                  val cross = graph.edges.count { group[it.i] != group[it.j] }
                  println(
                      "minWeight %.1f -> %4d edges, %3d crossing a group boundary, components > 1: %s"
                          .format(
                              cut,
                              graph.edges.size,
                              cross,
                              groups,
                          ),
                  )
                  val kept = edges.values().filter { it.weight > cut }
                  "w>%.1f  %de  %d groups".format(cut, graph.edges.size, groups.size) to
                      dynamicGraphFLines(state.points, kept, maxWeight = ceiling, colormap = "magma")
              }
          showPlaneGrid(
              *panels.toTypedArray(),
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 430,
              cellHeight = 430,
              window = dynamicGraphPlaneWindow(window),
          )
  - create:
      box: dgs_breathing
      name: "5 — LAUNCH ME: the graph rewiring while nothing moves"
      frame:
        x: 530.0
        y: 300.0
        w: 460.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          LAUNCH this box (animate/loop), do not just run it: animateEvolution returns a Frames,
          and a Frames that is only built never runs.

          The cloud NEVER MOVES. Every edge that appears or disappears is the anisotropic metric
          breathing -- an axis that rotates with the clock and a stretch along it between 0.25 and
          2.0. The right-hand panel is the control: same k, same cloud, same code path, clock
          pinned at zero, so it holds exactly 590 edges for all 420 steps.
          */
          val n = 260
          val cloud =
              List(n) { i ->
                  val a = i * 2.39996322972865332
                  val r = 0.5 * Math.sqrt((i + 0.5) / n)
                  Vec3((r * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (r * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          val window = dynamicGraphWindow(cloud, padFraction = 0.06)
          val ceiling = 1.2

          class Breath(
              val warped: DynamicPointState,
              val plain: DynamicPointState,
              val warpedEdges: DynamicEdgeList,
              val plainEdges: DynamicEdgeList,
              val hash: Vec3SpatialHash,
          )

          val warpedSystem = Vec3BreathingAnisotropicKnnSystem(
              k = 5,
              ttl = 0.25f,
              reinforce = 6.0,
              maxWeight = ceiling,
              mutualOnly = true,
              queryRadius = 0.13,
          )
          val plainSystem = Vec3BreathingAnisotropicKnnSystem(
              k = 5,
              ttl = 0.25f,
              reinforce = 6.0,
              maxWeight = ceiling,
              mutualOnly = true,
              queryRadius = 0.13,
          )

          val seed = Breath(
              DynamicPointState(cloud.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList()),
              DynamicPointState(cloud.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList()),
              DynamicEdgeList(n),
              DynamicEdgeList(n),
              Vec3SpatialHash(0.065),
          )

          animateEvolution(
              seed,
              totalSteps = 420,
              seconds = 8.0,
              columns = 2,
              cellSide = 460,
              framesTarget = 160,
              step = { s ->
                  stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(
                      1f / 60f,
                      s.warped,
                      s.warpedEdges,
                      s.hash,
                      warpedSystem,
                      2.5,
                  )
                  // The system advances state.time itself, so pinning it either side of the call is
                  // what "the same code with the time-dependence removed" means.
                  s.plain.time = 0f
                  stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(
                      1f / 60f,
                      s.plain,
                      s.plainEdges,
                      s.hash,
                      plainSystem,
                      2.5,
                  )
                  s.plain.time = 0f
                  s
              },
              panels = { s, step ->
                  [
                      "breathing, t=%.2fs, %d edges".format(s.warped.time, s.warpedEdges.values().size) to
                          dynamicGraphPanel(s.warped.points, s.warpedEdges.values(), window, 460, 460, ceiling, "magma"),
                      "frozen, step %d, %d edges".format(step, s.plainEdges.values().size) to
                          dynamicGraphPanel(s.plain.points, s.plainEdges.values(), window, 460, 460, ceiling, "magma"),
                  ]
              },
          )
  - create:
      box: dgs_morphogenesis
      name: "6 — LAUNCH ME: morphogenesis, and its tip-growth-off twin"
      frame:
        x: 1000.0
        y: 300.0
        w: 480.0
        h: 100.0
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          LAUNCH this box, do not just run it.

          The full pipeline: diffuse a resource along the edges and climb its gradient, relax the
          springs, grow tips where the incident edges pull coherently, merge what has collided,
          smooth, jitter. The right-hand panel is the same pipeline with ONE stage removed -- tip
          growth -- so the difference between the panels is that stage and nothing else.
          */
          val seedRing =
              List(64) { i ->
                  val a = 2.0 * Math.PI * i / 64
                  Vec3((0.42 * Math.cos(a)).toFloat(), (0.42 * Math.sin(a)).toFloat(), 0f)
              }
          // Sized for where the structure ENDS UP. Re-fitting per frame would make growth invisible.
          val window = doubleArrayOf(-0.95, -0.95, 0.95, 0.95)
          val ceiling = 3.0

          class Morph(
              val state: DynamicPointState,
              val kinetics: DynamicPointKinetics,
              val edges: DynamicEdgeList,
              val hash: Vec3SpatialHash,
              val pipeline: DynamicProcessPipeline,
              val system: DynamicGraphSystem,
          )

          fun morph(grow: Boolean): Morph {
              val state = DynamicPointState(seedRing.map { Vec3(it) }.toMutableList())
              val kinetics = DynamicPointKinetics(mutableListOf(), mutableListOf(), mutableListOf())
              kinetics.ensureSize(state.pointCount)
              // Seed the resource on a quarter of the ring, so chemotaxis has a gradient to climb.
              for (i in 0 until 16) kinetics.resource[i] = 6.0
              val stages = mutableListOf<DynamicPointProcess>(
                  SignalDiffusionAndChemotaxisProcess(diffusionRate = 0.5, chemoGain = 0.35, maxSpeed = 0.30),
                  // rest = restLengthTimesWeight / weight: 0.075 is a rest length of 0.05 at a typical
                  // weight of 1.5.
                  SpringMotionProcess(springK = 1.2, damping = 3.0, restLengthTimesWeight = 0.075, maxSpeed = 0.30),
              )
              if (grow)
                  stages +=
                      DirectedTipGrowthProcess(
                          coherenceThreshold = 1.6,
                          spawnDistance = 0.035,
                          localDensityRadius = 0.05,
                          localDensityMax = 6,
                          childEdgeWeight = 1.5,
                          childEdgeTtl = 1.5f,
                          maxWeight = ceiling,
                          maxPointCount = 900,
                      )
              stages += MergeClosePointsProcess(mergeDistance = 0.012, minCombinedWeight = 2.0)
              stages += RelaxToMidpointProcess(gain = 1.5)
              stages += JitterProcess(amplitude = 0.04)
              return Morph(
                  state,
                  kinetics,
                  DynamicEdgeList(state.pointCount),
                  Vec3SpatialHash(0.05),
                  DynamicProcessPipeline(stages),
                  Vec3PersistentProximityHysteresisSystem(
                      rEnter = 0.05,
                      rExit = 0.07,
                      ttl = 0.8f,
                      reinforce = 3.0,
                      maxWeight = ceiling,
                  ),
              )
          }

          animateEvolution(
              morph(grow = true) to morph(grow = false),
              totalSteps = 560,
              seconds = 10.0,
              columns = 2,
              cellSide = 490,
              framesTarget = 200,
              // Geometric: the 900-point cap is reached at step 79, so a linear schedule would spend
              // seven eighths of the clip on the aftermath. ramp = 25 puts the mid-point at step 93.
              ramp = 25.0,
              step = { (grown, flat) ->
                  for (m in [grown, flat]) {
                      stepDynamicGraphWithExponentialDecay(
                          1f / 60f,
                          m.state,
                          m.edges,
                          m.hash,
                          m.system,
                          0.6,
                      )
                      m.pipeline.step(1f / 60f, m.state, m.kinetics, m.edges, m.hash)
                  }
                  grown to flat
              },
              panels = { (grown, flat), step ->
                  [
                      "grow ON  s%d  %dpts %de"
                          .format(
                              step,
                              grown.state.pointCount,
                              grown.edges.values().size,
                          ) to dynamicGraphPanel(grown.state.points, grown.edges.values(), window, 490, 490, ceiling, "magma"),
                      "grow OFF  s%d  %dpts %de"
                          .format(
                              step,
                              flat.state.pointCount,
                              flat.edges.values().size,
                          ) to dynamicGraphPanel(flat.state.points, flat.edges.values(), window, 490, 490, ceiling, "magma"),
                  ]
              },
          )
  # Bare `execute` ops run each box's stored `code`. The four measuring boxes print the numbers this
  # family's page quotes and its tests assert. The two animating boxes are deliberately NOT executed
  # here: animateEvolution returns a Frames, which only runs when the box is launched, so executing
  # one would be a compile check dressed up as a demonstration. Launch them yourself.
  - execute:
      box: dgs_six_systems
  - execute:
      box: dgs_decay
  - execute:
      box: dgs_hysteresis
  - execute:
      box: dgs_threshold

before:
name: four_summary_pyramid
description: |
  A **summarised quadtree over a raster**, declared as one pass chain: three moving blobs, a 2×2
  reduction pyramid that carries mergeable statistics instead of colour, and an overlay that draws
  what each cell of the tree knows as a centroid and an ellipse. Three boxes — a renderer, a bundle,
  and one declaration.

  The structure is free. A 2×2 reduction has a parent for every four cells and one cell at the top,
  which *is* a complete quadtree — no nodes, no pointers, no subdivision criterion and no build step
  that can disagree with the data. `summary-value-0` is the root and `summary-value-8` is the leaf
  level, and a node at depth d is a texel of the d-th pass. What each cell carries is where this
  differs from the downsample pyramid in [four_pass_chain](#four_pass_chain): instead of an average
  colour, three planes of **sufficient statistics**.

    - `summary-value-d` — weight, value mean, value variance, occupancy.
    - `summary-moment-d` — Σwx, Σwy, Σwx², Σwy².
    - `summary-extent-d` — Σwxy, and the two extremes of the value.

  From the last two, `centroid = E[p]` and `covariance = E[ppᵀ] − E[p]E[p]ᵀ`, so every cell has an
  orientation and an anisotropy. That is the payoff the overlay draws: an adaptive cell stops saying
  "occupied" and starts carrying a crude geometric model of what is inside it — where the mass is,
  which way it runs, how elongated it is. Watch the ellipses lean as the blobs rotate.

  **And the statistics are what a descent is made of.** `adaptiveSummaryCells` walks the tree from
  depth 1 down, stopping wherever a cell already describes its contents well enough, and draws the
  cells it stopped at — big ones over empty space, small ones along the blobs' edges. That is the
  difference between a quadtree and a pyramid in the only sense that matters to a consumer: without
  a criterion every reader takes one level, and one level of a pyramid is a grid. A descent is also
  a pass chain in the same literal sense a Jacobi sweep is — two passes per level, at two different
  resolutions, because the decision lives at the tree's scale and the drawing at the picture's.

  **Every channel is a per-cell mean rather than a sum**, and that is not a compromise. A sum over a
  256² image leaves 0..1 immediately and a channel outside 0..1 cannot be read back at all, while
  every statistic that matters — centroid, covariance, mean, variance — is a ratio in which the
  cell's area cancels. A mean also merges by averaging four children, which is one `+` per channel
  with a `0.25` on the end.

  Things worth trying in the summary box:

    - `threshold` on the cut, from `0.02f` up to `0.4f` and down to `0.005f`. The cells coarsen and
      refine as one; at the coarse end the whole cut collapses towards depth 1 and you can see it is
      a *tiling* rather than a set of cells that happen not to overlap.
    - `criterion`, between `OCCUPANCY`, `SPREAD`, `CENTROID_OFFSET` and `VALUE_VARIANCE`. Four

  reduction pyramid that carries mergeable statistics instead of colour, and an overlay that draws
  what each cell of the tree knows as a centroid and an ellipse. Three boxes — a renderer, a bundle,

  that can disagree with the data. `summary-value-0` is the root and `summary-value-8` is the leaf

  colour, three planes of **sufficient statistics**.

  orientation and an anisotropy. That is the payoff the overlay draws: an adaptive cell stops saying
  "occupied" and starts carrying a crude geometric model of what is inside it — where the mass is,
  which way it runs, how elongated it is. Watch the ellipses lean as the blobs rotate.
