                  for (parent in level) {
                      val children = word[cursor++].coerceAtMost(slots)
                      val step = parent.dur / PatQ.of(slots)
                      val on = bjorklund(children, slots).withIndex().filter { it.value }.map { it.index }
                      on.forEachIndexed { k, slot ->
                          val start = parent.start + step * PatQ.of(slot)
                          val end = if (k + 1 < on.size) parent.start + step * PatQ.of(on[k + 1]) else parent.end
                          next += PatArc(start, end)
                      }
                  }
                  level = next
                  levels += level
              }
              return levels
          }

          fun asPat(arcs: List<PatArc>, name: String = "bd") = fromCycle { sub ->
              arcs.mapNotNull { arc -> arc.intersect(sub)?.let { PatEvent(it, name, whole = arc) } }
          }

          val t = tile(depth, slots, a, b)

          // The word starts on a 1, so R1 is R0 held - the first branch that splits anything is R2.
          showPatRollOf(
              *t.mapIndexed { n, level -> "R$n (${level.size})" to asPat(level) }.toTypedArray(),
              title = "each pulse subdivides into ${a} or ${b} on a ${slots}-slot grid",
              cycles = 1,
              channel = "tree",
          )

          /*
          The rings as hierarchical pulse levels: one voice per level, so every hit of a fine level
          sits inside exactly one hit of the level above it.
          Coarse loud, fine quiet. Every coarse onset is also a fine onset - that is what a tree means -
          so at equal gain all four voices land together on the strong hits and the hierarchy turns into
          a pile. The gain ramp makes it foreground and background instead. Short samples for the same
          reason: sd:2 and click decay before the next level arrives.
          */
          val voices = ["bd" to 1.0, "sd:2" to 0.7, "hh:2" to 0.45, "click" to 0.35]
          val played = t.takeLast(voices.size)
          val music = stack(
              *played
                  .mapIndexed { i, level ->
                      asPat(level, voices[i].first) with gain(voices[i].second)
                  }
                  .toTypedArray(),
          )

          showPatRollOf(
              *played
                  .mapIndexed { i, level ->
                      "${voices[i].first} (${level.size})" to asPat(level, voices[i].first)
                  }
                  .toTypedArray(),
              title = "the last four levels, one voice each",
              cycles = 2,
              channel = "levels",
          )
          val dirt = showDirtAudio(music, cycles = 8, cps = 1.0, channel = "audio") // real samples, not patVoice
          val audio = dirt.audio
          val wav = "kolakoski-tree-${slots}-${a}${b}-d$depth.wav".file
          afield.audio.engine.WavFloatArrayWriter.writeStereo16(wav, audio.left, audio.right, PatSoundDocs.SR, 0.9f)
          println("wrote $wav — samples: ${dirt.usedSamples}, matched ${dirt.matched}, synth fallback ${dirt.unmatched}")

          markdown(
              "main",
              """
          ### Level sizes: ${t.joinToString(", ") { it.size.toString() }}

          Those are the partial sums of the Kolakoski word - each level eats as many terms as the level
          above it has pulses, and the sum of those terms is the next level's size.
          """,
          )

          displayOpen("tree")
          displayOpen("audio")
          displayOpen("levels")
          displayOpen("main")
  - create:
      box: wav_on_canvas
      name: 3 - a wav on the canvas
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 392.0, w: 393.5, h: 136.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          3 - A player that lives on the canvas, not in an output.

          showPatAudio puts an <audio> in the box's OUTPUT, which is recomputed every run and is not
          saved with the document. `customization` is a box property - JS run against the box's own
          element on the canvas, and it IS saved - so an audio element appended there is part of the
          document: reopen it tomorrow, press play, no run needed.

          POKE THIS: change the pattern. Keep the clip short - it travels as base64 inside the document,
          so ~4s of stereo is ~700KB of property. cps is low because the bar is 24 slots wide: see the
          tempo note in kolakoski_x_euclid.
          */
          val counts = kolakoskiWord(8)
          val hybrid = pat(counts.joinToString(" ") { "[bd($it,3)]" })

          val dirt = patRenderStereoDirt(hybrid, cycles = 2, cps = 0.35) // 5.7s; 24-slot bar, so 4.2 hits/s
          val rendered = dirt.audio
          val bytes = afield.audio.engine.WavFloatArrayWriter.encodeStereo16(
              rendered.left,
              rendered.right,
              PatSoundDocs.SR,
              0.9f,
          )

          // The file on disk, for dragging into an editor...
          val wav = "kolakoski-canvas.wav".file
          wav.writeBytes(bytes)

          // ...and the same bytes pinned into this box on the canvas.
          val b64 = java.util.Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(bytes)
          customization =
              """
              this.style.background = "var(--field-bg)"
              if (!this.querySelector("audio.field-wav")) {
                  this.insertAdjacentHTML("beforeend",
                      "<audio class='field-wav' controls style='width:100%'></audio>")
              }
              this.querySelector("audio.field-wav").src = "data:audio/wav;base64,$b64"
          """

          println("${bytes.size / 1024}KB of wav, on the canvas and at $wav — samples: ${dirt.usedSamples} ${dirt.matched}")
  - launch: { box: kolakoski_x_euclid, property: code }
  - launch: { box: kolakoski_tree, property: code }
  - launch: { box: wav_on_canvas, property: code }
  - await: { wait: pending }

before:
name: morpho_circuit_search
description: >
  Loadable demo of the MorphoHDL circuit-search layer — afield.morpho/MorphoSpec.kt (oracle, cost
  model, evaluator), MorphoGenome.kt + MorphoGenerator.kt (programs as MorphoHDL source text, and
  the mutations that make new ones), MorphoSearch.kt (random / hill climb / (mu+lambda) evolution /
  a width curriculum), MorphoProblems.kt (the named questions) and MorphoSearchFLines.kt (the two
  vector figures). Three pure-compute boxes, no Window and no Renderer: everything goes through
  showPlaneGrid, which is drawToSVG then display(), so no AWT and no GPU.

  Every candidate any of these boxes evaluates is compiled by *morpho's own* compiler on GraalJS
  and run by MorphoSim. Nothing here models a circuit; the search's fitness function is the real
  toolchain, which is why anything it finds is a MorphoHDL program you can paste into a morpho box.

    1. morpho_search_control  — the control experiment. A one-bit full adder, searched for as
                    straight-line logic over morpho's eight standard cells, checked against the
                    complete eight-row truth table. Random sampling, hill climbing and evolution
                    all get 4000 compiler invocations from the same generator with the same seed;
                    two of them find it and the control does not, and the convergence figure draws
                    all three on one set of axes so the claim is a gap between curves rather than a
                    number in prose. Prints the program it found: Xor3 and Maj3, which is exactly
                    what tiny_morpho.py's full_adder is.
    2. morpho_search_recursion — the positive structural result. Reduce an N-bit bus to one bit.
                    Morpho broadcasts a LUT across a bus, so *no* combination of gates narrows one
                    — the only route from eight wires to one is to keep SPLITting — which makes
                    every correct answer here genuinely divide-and-conquer. Selected at widths 2,
                    3 and 5 — an odd family on purpose, see MorphoProblems.ODD_FAMILY — and then
                    re-compiled at 7, 16, 32 and 48 bits, widths nothing was selected on, and drawn
                    at three of them as real circuits through MorphoFLines. It is the same source
                    text at every width; that is what parametric means in this language. The second
                    figure is the (gates, depth) Pareto front over every correct design both runs
                    produced, which is small and is not empty: a reduction can be a shallow wide
                    tree or a deep cheap one and the search finds both ends.
    3. morpho_search_adder    — the negative result, which is the more interesting half. Nobody
                    finds a recursive ripple adder, with or without the two SPLITs given, at any
                    budget tried. The box proves the target is *in* the search space by writing the
                    skeleton by hand in the generator's own grammar and scoring it (16 gates,
                    depth 8 — exactly ripple_adder), then shows the plateau every driver stops on
                    and a cost figure whose only occupants are the two hand-written designs.

  Replay this file into a fresh Field with the agent backdoor (field_run_transcript) to see all
  three, then turn a budget up, swap a driver, change the width family, or point MorphoProblems at
  a different oracle and re-run a box. Each `execute` op omits inline code, so it runs the box's
  stored `code` property. The page is public/docs/morpho_search.md.
operations:
  - create:
      box: morpho_search_control
      name: Does selection beat sampling? One-bit full adder, three drivers, one budget
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 60.0, w: 600.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.lang.morpho.*

          /*
          The whole layer in four lines: a problem is an oracle plus a width family plus a
          grammar, and a driver turns a budget into a program. Nothing about addition is supplied
          except `sum, c_out = a + b + c_in`; the parts list is morpho's own eight standard cells,
          lifted out of tiny_morpho.py rather than copied into Kotlin.
          */
          val problem = MorphoProblems.fullAdderCell()
          val budget = 4000
          println(problem)
          println("palette: " + MorphoPalette.standard.luts.joinToString { it.name })
          println(
              "input space at 1 bit: ${problem.spec.inputSpace(1)} vectors, " + "exhaustive = ${problem.spec.isExhaustiveAt(1)}",
          )

          // Same generator, same seed, same budget. One unit of budget is one invocation of
          // morpho's compiler, which is the only resource all three spend at comparable rates.
          val runs = listOf(
              MorphoSearch.random(problem.spec, problem.generator, budget, seed = 2),
              MorphoSearch.hillClimb(problem.spec, problem.generator, budget, seed = 2),
              MorphoSearch.evolve(problem.spec, problem.generator, budget, seed = 2),
          )
          runs.forEach { println(it.summary()) }

          // What was actually found, in MorphoHDL. This is paste-into-a-morpho-box text.
          runs
              .firstOrNull { it.solved }
              ?.best
              ?.let { winner ->
                  println()
                  println(winner.genome.phenotype().cells[0].render())
                  println("cost: ${winner.fitness.cost}")
              }

          /*
          The control arm IS the figure: cyan is random sampling, orange the hill climb, green
          the population. A dropped tick marks the invocation at which a run first became exactly
          correct, because at this scale a curve that reaches zero and one that reaches 0.004
          look identical and that is the entire question.
          */
          showPlaneGrid(
              "one-bit full adder — best-so-far bit error vs compiler invocations (log x, $budget budget)\n" +
                  morphoRunCaption(runs) to morphoConvergenceFLines(runs),
              columns = 1,
              cellWidth = 700,
              cellHeight = 420,
              window = morphoPlotWindow(),
          )
  - create:
      box: morpho_search_recursion
      name: A recursion, found — reducing a bus to one bit, then drawn at three widths
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 520.0, w: 590.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.lang.morpho.*

          /*
          y = (x != 0). The reason this is the interesting target and bitwise XOR is not: morpho
          sizes a LUT cell to its widest operand and broadcasts the narrow ones, so there is no
          gate and no combination of gates that turns eight wires into one. The only way down is
          SPLIT, which means every correct answer is divide-and-conquer by construction.
          */
          val problem = MorphoProblems.orReduce()
          println(problem)

          val runs = listOf(
              MorphoSearch.random(problem.spec, problem.generator, 6000, seed = 2),
              MorphoSearch.evolve(problem.spec, problem.generator, 6000, seed = 2, mu = 24, lambda = 40),
          )
          runs.forEach { println(it.summary()) }

          // Cheapest correct design across both runs; if a seed happens not to solve it, fall back
          // to the closest thing found rather than throwing -- this is a demo, not an assertion.
          val correct = runs.mapNotNull { it.best }.filter { it.fitness.correct }
          val best = correct.minByOrNull { it.gates } ?: runs.mapNotNull { it.best }.first()
          println()
          println(if (correct.isEmpty()) "(nothing exactly correct this run; showing the best found)" else "")
          println(best.genome.phenotype().cells[0].render())

          /*
          Selected at 2, 3 and 5 -- an ODD family on purpose. SPLIT gives equal halves exactly
          when the width is even, so a family of powers of two never shows the search a cell
          whose two halves differ, and it will happily return a design that is silently wrong at
          5, 7 and 9. Re-compiled here at widths nothing was selected on: same source text, new
          signature, nothing to translate and nothing to get wrong.
          */
          listOf(7, 9, 16, 32, 48).forEach { w ->
              val f = MorphoSearch.generalization(best.genome, problem.spec, listOf(w))
              println("  at %2d bits: %s".format(w, f))
          }

          /*
          The Pareto front over every correct design the two runs produced. It is small and it is
          not empty: a reduction can be a shallow wide tree or a deep cheap one, and the search
          finds both ends. The staircase is drawn as a step function on purpose -- there is no
          design at a fractional gate count, and a smooth curve would claim there is.
          */
          val found = runs.flatMap { it.costPoints() }
          println()
          println(
              "Pareto front (gates, depth) at %d bits: %s"
                  .format(
                      problem.spec.widths.max(),
                      runs.flatMap { it.front }.joinToString(", ") { "(${it.gates}, ${it.depth})" },
                  ),
          )

          /*
          And the circuits themselves, through the same MorphoFLines the rest of the page uses.
          One source, three signatures, three different circuits: that is the language's whole
          conceit and it now applies to a design nobody wrote.
          */
          val source = best.genome.render()
          val panels =
              listOf(4, 8, 16).map { w ->
                  val c = morphoCircuit(MorphoProblems.ROOT, w, source = source)
                  c.growFully(relaxSteps = 220)
                  "evolved or-reduce at %d bits — %d gates, depth %d".format(w, c.netlist.gateCount, c.depth.toInt()) to
                      c.flines(fit = true)
              }
          showPlaneGrid(
              *panels.toTypedArray(),
              columns = 3,
              cellWidth = 300,
              cellHeight = 300,
              window = morphoUnitWindow(),
          )

          showPlaneGrid(
              "or-reduce — best-so-far bit error vs compiler invocations (log x)\n" + morphoRunCaption(runs) to
                  morphoConvergenceFLines(runs),
              "cost of an or-reduce — depth (x) against gates (y)\n" +
                  "${found.size} correct designs, ${runs.sumOf { it.front.size }} of them non-dominated. " +
                  "A staircase is only drawn when the front has more than one point: for a reduction " +
                  "it usually does not, because cheaper and shallower go together here" to morphoParetoFLines(found),
              channel = "cost",
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 430,
              cellHeight = 380,
              window = morphoPlotWindow(),
          )
  - create:
      box: morpho_search_adder
      name: The recursive adder is not found — and the target is provably in the space
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 1020.0, w: 590.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.lang.morpho.*

          // The result this branch set out to get, and did not. Reported because the alternative is
          // to quietly not mention it.
          val free = MorphoProblems.recursiveAdder()
          val guided = MorphoProblems.guidedRecursiveAdder()
          val budget = 6000
          val runs = listOf(
              MorphoSearch.random(free.spec, free.generator, budget, seed = 1),
              MorphoSearch.hillClimb(free.spec, free.generator, budget, seed = 1),
              MorphoSearch.evolve(free.spec, free.generator, budget, seed = 1),
              MorphoSearch.evolve(
                  guided.spec,
                  guided.generator,
                  budget,
                  seed = 1,
                  label = "evolution, SPLITs given",
              ),
          )
          runs.forEach { println(it.summary()) }

          /*
          A negative result is only worth printing if the thing not found was findable. Here is
          the ripple skeleton, written by hand in exactly the grammar the generator emits, scored
          by exactly the evaluator the search used.
          */
          val target = MorphoGenome(
              listOf(
                  MorphoCellGenome(
                      name = MorphoProblems.ROOT,
                      inputs = listOf("a", "b", "c"),
                      statements = listOf(
                          MorphoStatement(listOf("a0", "a1"), "SPLIT", listOf("a")),
                          MorphoStatement(listOf("b0", "b1"), "SPLIT", listOf("b")),
                          MorphoStatement(listOf("s0", "cm"), MorphoProblems.ROOT, listOf("a0", "b0", "c")),
                          MorphoStatement(listOf("s1", "co"), MorphoProblems.ROOT, listOf("a1", "b1", "cm")),
                          MorphoStatement(listOf("sum"), "CAT", listOf("s0", "s1")),
                      ),
                      outputs = listOf("sum", "co"),
                      fallback = "full_adder",
                  ),
              ),
              free.generator.preamble,
          )
          println()
          println(target.cells[0].render())
          println("  scored at 2/4/8: " + MorphoEvaluator(free.spec).evaluate(target.render(), target.rootName))
          println("  at 16 bits:      " + MorphoSearch.generalization(target, free.spec, listOf(16)))
          println("  at 32 bits:      " + MorphoSearch.generalization(target, free.spec, listOf(32)))

          // What the humans cost, through the same evaluator rather than quoted from a paper.
          val references =
              listOf("ripple_adder", "brent_kung_adder").mapNotNull { design ->
                  free.reference(design).cost?.let { MorphoCostPoint(design, it.gates, it.depth, reference = true) }
              }
          references.forEach { println("  reference ${it.label}: ${it.gates} gates, depth ${it.depth}") }

          /*
          Left: four flat tails, none of which reaches zero. Right: the cost plane for an 8-bit
          adder, occupied entirely by the two designs a person wrote. The empty half of that
          panel is the finding.
          */
          val found = runs.flatMap { it.costPoints() }
          println("correct designs found by any driver: ${found.size}")
          showPlaneGrid(
              "recursive 8-bit adder — best-so-far bit error vs compiler invocations (log x)\n" + morphoRunCaption(runs) to
                  morphoConvergenceFLines(runs),
              "cost of an 8-bit adder — depth (x) against gates (y)\n" +
                  "cyan: morpho's own designs.  orange: everything the search found (${found.size})" to
                  morphoParetoFLines(found + references),
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 430,
              cellHeight = 400,
              window = morphoPlotWindow(),
          )
  - execute:
      box: morpho_search_control
  - execute:
      box: morpho_search_recursion
  - execute:
      box: morpho_search_adder

          5, 7 and 9. Re-compiled here at widths nothing was selected on: same source text, new
          signature, nothing to translate and nothing to get wrong.
          */
          [7, 9, 16, 32, 48].forEach { w ->
              val f = MorphoSearch.generalization(best.genome, problem.spec, [w])
              println("  at %2d bits: %s".format(w, f))
          }

          /*
          The Pareto front over every correct design the two runs produced. It is small and it is
          not empty: a reduction can be a shallow wide tree or a deep cheap one, and the search
          finds both ends. The staircase is drawn as a step function on purpose -- there is no
          design at a fractional gate count, and a smooth curve would claim there is.
          */
          val found = runs.flatMap { it.costPoints() }
          println()
          println(
              "Pareto front (gates, depth) at %d bits: %s"
                  .format(
                      problem.spec.widths.max(),
                      runs.flatMap { it.front }.joinToString(", ") { "(${it.gates}, ${it.depth})" },
                  ),
          )

          /*
          And the circuits themselves, through the same MorphoFLines the rest of the page uses.
          One source, three signatures, three different circuits: that is the language's whole
          conceit and it now applies to a design nobody wrote.
          */
          val source = best.genome.render()
          val panels =
              [4, 8, 16].map { w ->
                  val c = morphoCircuit(MorphoProblems.ROOT, w, source = source)
                  c.growFully(relaxSteps = 220)
                  "evolved or-reduce at %d bits — %d gates, depth %d".format(w, c.netlist.gateCount, c.depth.toInt()) to
                      c.flines(fit = true)
              }
          showPlaneGrid(
              *panels.toTypedArray(),
              columns = 3,
              cellWidth = 300,
              cellHeight = 300,
              window = morphoUnitWindow(),
          )

          showPlaneGrid(
              "or-reduce — best-so-far bit error vs compiler invocations (log x)\n" + morphoRunCaption(runs) to
                  morphoConvergenceFLines(runs),
              "cost of an or-reduce — depth (x) against gates (y)\n" +
                  "${found.size} correct designs, ${runs.sumOf { it.front.size }} of them non-dominated. " +
                  "A staircase is only drawn when the front has more than one point: for a reduction " +
                  "it usually does not, because cheaper and shallower go together here" to morphoParetoFLines(found),
              channel = "cost",
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 430,
              cellHeight = 380,
              window = morphoPlotWindow(),
          )
  - create:
      box: morpho_search_adder
      name: The recursive adder is not found — and the target is provably in the space
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 1020.0, w: 590.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.lang.morpho.*

          // The result this branch set out to get, and did not. Reported because the alternative is
          // to quietly not mention it.
          val free = MorphoProblems.recursiveAdder()
          val guided = MorphoProblems.guidedRecursiveAdder()
          val budget = 6000
          val runs = [
              MorphoSearch.random(free.spec, free.generator, budget, seed = 1),
              MorphoSearch.hillClimb(free.spec, free.generator, budget, seed = 1),
              MorphoSearch.evolve(free.spec, free.generator, budget, seed = 1),
              MorphoSearch.evolve(
                  guided.spec,
                  guided.generator,
                  budget,
                  seed = 1,
                  label = "evolution, SPLITs given",
              ),
          ]
          runs.forEach { println(it.summary()) }

          /*
          A negative result is only worth printing if the thing not found was findable. Here is
          the ripple skeleton, written by hand in exactly the grammar the generator emits, scored
          by exactly the evaluator the search used.
          */
          val target = MorphoGenome(
              [
                  MorphoCellGenome(
                      name = MorphoProblems.ROOT,
                      inputs = ["a", "b", "c"],
                      statements = [
                          MorphoStatement(["a0", "a1"], "SPLIT", ["a"]),
                          MorphoStatement(["b0", "b1"], "SPLIT", ["b"]),
                          MorphoStatement(["s0", "cm"], MorphoProblems.ROOT, ["a0", "b0", "c"]),
                          MorphoStatement(["s1", "co"], MorphoProblems.ROOT, ["a1", "b1", "cm"]),
                          MorphoStatement(["sum"], "CAT", ["s0", "s1"]),
                      ],
                      outputs = ["sum", "co"],
                      fallback = "full_adder",
                  ),
              ],
              free.generator.preamble,
          )
          println()
          println(target.cells[0].render())
          println("  scored at 2/4/8: " + MorphoEvaluator(free.spec).evaluate(target.render(), target.rootName))
          println("  at 16 bits:      " + MorphoSearch.generalization(target, free.spec, [16]))
          println("  at 32 bits:      " + MorphoSearch.generalization(target, free.spec, [32]))

          // What the humans cost, through the same evaluator rather than quoted from a paper.
          val references =
              ["ripple_adder", "brent_kung_adder"].mapNotNull { design ->
                  free.reference(design).cost?.let { MorphoCostPoint(design, it.gates, it.depth, reference = true) }
              }
          references.forEach { println("  reference ${it.label}: ${it.gates} gates, depth ${it.depth}") }

          /*
          Left: four flat tails, none of which reaches zero. Right: the cost plane for an 8-bit
          adder, occupied entirely by the two designs a person wrote. The empty half of that
          panel is the finding.
          */
          val found = runs.flatMap { it.costPoints() }
          println("correct designs found by any driver: ${found.size}")
          showPlaneGrid(
              "recursive 8-bit adder — best-so-far bit error vs compiler invocations (log x)\n" + morphoRunCaption(runs) to
                  morphoConvergenceFLines(runs),
              "cost of an 8-bit adder — depth (x) against gates (y)\n" +
                  "cyan: morpho's own designs.  orange: everything the search found (${found.size})" to
                  morphoParetoFLines(found + references),
              columns = 2,
              cellWidth = 430,
              cellHeight = 400,
              window = morphoPlotWindow(),
          )
  - execute:
      box: morpho_search_control
  - execute:
      box: morpho_search_recursion
  - execute:
      box: morpho_search_adder

before: name: onnx_webcam_live description: > One box: grab a webcam frame, run Depth Anything V2 and CLIP on it, and show the frame beside its depth map with a zero-shot ranking over four text prompts. Press the run key again for a new frame. operations: - create: box: onnx_webcam name: Webcam perception frame: x: 80.0 y: 80.0 w: 360.0 h: 100.0 properties: code: | import afield.ai.inference.onnx.ClipImage import afield.ai.inference.onnx.DepthAnything import afield.ai.inference.onnx.clipEncode import afield.media.image.util.PngEncoder import java.nio.ByteBuffer import java.nio.ByteOrder import org.bytedeco.javacv.OpenCVFrameConverter import org.bytedeco.javacv.OpenCVFrameGrabber import org.bytedeco.opencv.global.opencv_imgproc.COLOR_BGR2RGBA import org.bytedeco.opencv.global.opencv_imgproc.COLOR_BGRA2RGBA import org.bytedeco.opencv.global.opencv_imgproc.COLOR_GRAY2RGBA import org.bytedeco.opencv.global.opencv_imgproc.cvtColor import org.bytedeco.opencv.opencv_core.Mat import org.lwjgl.system.MemoryUtil // Encoded once, here, into a val: the text tower is not in the per-frame path. First call in // a session loads the 242MB encoder; after that each prompt is a few milliseconds. val prompts = mapOf( "a person at a desk" to clipEncode("a person sitting at a desk"), "an empty room" to clipEncode("an empty room"), "a close-up face" to clipEncode("a close-up of a face"), "a hand up close" to clipEncode("a hand held up to the camera"), ) val grabber = OpenCVFrameGrabber(0) grabber.start() try { val conv = OpenCVFrameConverter.ToMat() // Discard the first few frames: auto-exposure and white balance need a moment, and // frame 0 is often black even on a camera that is working perfectly. var mat: Mat? = null repeat(8) { grabber.grab()?.let { f -> mat = conv.convert(f) } } val m = requireNotNull(mat) { "camera delivered no frame — on macOS check Privacy & Security > Camera for the app " + "that launched Field, and restart it (a cached denial survives until you do)" } val w = m.cols() val h = m.rows() val rgbaMat = Mat() when (m.channels()) { 4 -> cvtColor(m, rgbaMat, COLOR_BGRA2RGBA) 3 -> cvtColor(m, rgbaMat, COLOR_BGR2RGBA) else -> cvtColor(m, rgbaMat, COLOR_GRAY2RGBA) } val bytes = w * h * 4 /* JavaCPP leaves Mat.data()'s capacity unset, so asByteBuffer() hands back an EMPTY buffer and a bounds-checked copy silently moves nothing -- which looks exactly like a black camera. Wrap the raw address instead, as WebcamTexture.copyMatToBuffer does. */ val src = MemoryUtil.memByteBuffer(rgbaMat.data().address(), bytes) val rgba = ByteBuffer.allocateDirect(bytes).order(ByteOrder.nativeOrder()) rgba.put(src.duplicate()) rgba.rewind() rgbaMat.release() // adaptation = 1f: normalise against this frame's own range, since each press is a // fresh start rather than a continuous stream. val depth = DepthAnything(width = 266, height = 266, adaptation = 1f) val stats = depth.infer(rgba, w, h) val embedding = ClipImage().encode(rgba, w, h) val ranked = embedding.classify(prompts) // Camera frame beside its depth map, both scaled to 360 tall. val outH = 360 val camOutW = (w.toDouble() / h * outH).toInt() val depthOutW = outH val outW = camOutW + depthOutW val px = IntArray(outW * outH) for (y in 0 until outH) { val sy = (y.toDouble() / outH * h).toInt().coerceIn(0, h - 1) for (x in 0 until camOutW) { val sx = (x.toDouble() / camOutW * w).toInt().coerceIn(0, w - 1) val o = (sy * w + sx) shl 2 val r = rgba.get(o).toInt() and 0xff val g = rgba.get(o + 1).toInt() and 0xff val b = rgba.get(o + 2).toInt() and 0xff px[y * outW + x] = (0xff shl 24) or (r shl 16) or (g shl 8) or b } } val d = depth.depthFp16.asShortBuffer() for (y in 0 until outH) { val sy = (y.toDouble() / outH * depth.height).toInt().coerceIn(0, depth.height - 1) for (x in 0 until depthOutW) { val sx = (x.toDouble() / depthOutW * depth.width).toInt().coerceIn(0, depth.width - 1) val t = ai.onnxruntime.platform.Fp16Conversions.fp16ToFloat(d.get(sy * depth.width + sx)).coerceIn(0f, 1f) val r = (255 * (t * 1.6f).coerceIn(0f, 1f)).toInt() val g = (255 * ((t - 0.25f) * 1.6f).coerceIn(0f, 1f)).toInt() val b = (255 * ((t - 0.6f) * 2.2f).coerceIn(0f, 1f)).toInt() px[y * outW + camOutW + x] = (0xff shl 24) or (r shl 16) or (g shl 8) or b } } val b64 = java.util.Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(PngEncoder.encode(px, outW, outH)) // `bar(max = 1.0)` so the bars read as "of the whole", not "of the best one this // frame" — a top-1 at 12% should look like 12%, not like a full bar. val top = Table(listOf("label", "confidence")) .rows(ranked.map { (label, p) -> listOf(label, p) }) .role("confidence", CellRole.ACCENT) .bar("confidence", max = 1.0, width = 180) .format("confidence") { "%.1f%%".format((it as Number).toDouble() * 100) } markdown( "main", """ {muted:${w}x$h · depth ${depth.lastInferenceMs}ms, raw [${"%.2f".format(stats.rawMin)}, ${"%.2f".format(stats.rawMax)}] · brighter = nearer} ${top.h} """, ) println( "depth ${depth.lastInferenceMs}ms best=${ranked.first().first} ${"%.1f".format(ranked.first().second * 100)}%", ) } finally { runCatching { grabber.stop() } runCatching { grabber.release() } } - before:
name: path_tracing_medium
description: |
  **Shafts of light through haze.** Two boxes: a renderer, and a slatted strip light over a hazed
  room whose `mediumDensity` cycles through four values every 192 samples, so the same geometry is
  drawn clear, thin and thick, over and over.
  
  A participating medium is the case where "the light travels in straight lines between surfaces"
  stops being true: the integrator has to sample a scattering event *along* the ray, and the visible
  result is the beam itself rather than only what it lands on. Cycling the density rather than
  picking one is what makes the difference legible — the geometry never moves, so everything that
  changes between passes is the medium.
  
  `dev_docs/PARTICIPATING_MEDIA.md` is the write-up, and the saved document at
  `dev_docs/agents/demos/path_tracing_medium/` is this same scene.
operations:
  - create:
      box: pt_renderer
      name: path tracing renderer
      frame: { x: 40.0, y: 40.0, w: 320.0, h: 110.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options

          prop<Window>(window)
          prop<Renderer>(renderer)
          Options.enableHDR = false
          once.renderer {
              window = Window("Field · participating medium")
              Renderer(window)
          }
          start(renderer::run)
  - create:
      box: pt_medium
      name: shafts of light through haze
      frame: { x: 320.0, y: 180.0, w: 400.0, h: 140.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.PathTraceEnvironment
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.PathTraceMaterial
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.PathTraceScene
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.PathTracingRenderer
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Camera

          prop<PathTracingRenderer>(tracer)

          /*
          A bright strip light with four slats under it, and nothing else lit. Everything is
          extruded along z and the camera looks down z, so the light's fan is seen in
          cross-section: shafts, and shadows between them.
          */
          val scene = PathTraceScene().apply {
              val floor = material(PathTraceMaterial.diffuse(0.32f, 0.30f, 0.27f))
              val wall = material(PathTraceMaterial.diffuse(0.16f, 0.17f, 0.21f))
              val slat = material(PathTraceMaterial.diffuse(0.10f, 0.09f, 0.08f))
              val lamp = material(PathTraceMaterial.emissive(340f, 300f, 230f))
              val ball = material(PathTraceMaterial.plastic(0.78f, 0.76f, 0.72f, 0.30f))
              quad(Vector3f(-6f, 0f, -4f), Vector3f(-6f, 0f, 4f), Vector3f(6f, 0f, 4f), Vector3f(6f, 0f, -4f), floor)
              quad(Vector3f(-6f, 0f, -4f), Vector3f(-6f, 5.4f, -4f), Vector3f(6f, 5.4f, -4f), Vector3f(6f, 0f, -4f), wall)
              quad(
                  Vector3f(-0.16f, 4.9f, -3.6f),
                  Vector3f(0.16f, 4.9f, -3.6f),
                  Vector3f(0.16f, 4.9f, 3.6f),
                  Vector3f(-0.16f, 4.9f, 3.6f),
                  lamp,
              )
              for (x in listOf(-1.75f, -0.62f, 0.62f, 1.75f)) {
                  quad(
                      Vector3f(x - 0.26f, 3.5f, -3.6f),
                      Vector3f(x + 0.26f, 3.5f, -3.6f),
                      Vector3f(x + 0.26f, 3.5f, 3.6f),
                      Vector3f(x - 0.26f, 3.5f, 3.6f),
                      slat,
                  )
              }
              sphere(Vector3f(1.5f, 0.85f, 0.6f), 0.85f, ball, 40, 20)
          }
          val camera = Camera(renderer).also {
              it.at.set(0.15f, 2.35f, 9.2f)
              it.target.set(0.15f, 2.25f, 0f)
              it.p.fov = 0.82
          }
          tracer = PathTracingRenderer(
              renderer,
              scene,
              PathTraceEnvironment.constant(0f),
              800,
              500,
              camera,
              name = "medium-demo",
          )
          tracer.maxBounces = 8
          tracer.samplesPerFrame = 2
          tracer.showEnvironment = false
          tracer.background = Vector4f(0f, 0f, 0f, 1f)
          tracer.exposure = 0.22f

          /*
          ---- the medium. Bounds matter: an unbounded medium has zero transmittance to
          ---- infinity, which would make an environment map unreachable. Here the box is
          ---- the room, so rays leaving it are simply out of the haze.
          */
          tracer.mediumBounds = Vector3f(-6f, 0f, -3.9f) to Vector3f(6f, 5.2f, 3.9f)
          tracer.mediumAlbedo = Vector3f(0.96f, 0.95f, 0.93f)
          tracer.mediumAnisotropy = 0.4f
          tracer.mediumDensity = 0.16f

          tracer.install()
          tracer.blitToScreen()
          println(
              "${tracer.emitterCount} emissive triangles of ${tracer.triangleCount}; " +
                  "the medium is ${tracer.mediumDensity} per world unit, albedo ${tracer.mediumAlbedo}, " +
                  "g ${tracer.mediumAnisotropy}",
          )

          /*
          ---- MOVE THIS ONE PARAMETER: mediumDensity. -----------------------------------
          The loop cycles it every 192 samples and prints the value. At 0.0 you get the room
          with hard-edged pools of light on the floor and nothing in the air. As it rises the
          shafts between the slats appear, the lamp gains a halo, and the far wall goes soft.
          Past about 0.35 the haze starts to swallow the geometry -- and because every collision
          spends one of maxBounces, the image also darkens there unless you raise it.

          Try mediumAnisotropy next: 0.8 pulls the glow into a tight forward halo around the
          lamp, -0.8 throws it back toward the camera and flattens the shafts.
          Comment out the frames block to hold one setting.
          */
          frames {
              while (true) {
                  for (density in listOf(0.0f, 0.08f, 0.16f, 0.40f)) {
                      tracer.mediumDensity = density
                      println("mediumDensity = $density")
                      // Changing it resets accumulation, but not until the next frame is recorded,
                      // so wait for the old budget to fall away before waiting for the new one.
                      while (tracer.samples >= 192) frame()
                      while (tracer.samples < 192) frame()
                  }
              }
          }
  - connect: { parent: pt_renderer, child: pt_medium }
  - launch: { box: pt_renderer, property: code, strand: renderer }
  - await: {}
  - execute: { box: pt_medium, property: code }
  - await: {}

          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.PathTraceMaterial
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.PathTraceScene
          import afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.PathTracingRenderer
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Camera

          prop<PathTracingRenderer>(tracer)

          /*
          A bright strip light with four slats under it, and nothing else lit. Everything is
          extruded along z and the camera looks down z, so the light's fan is seen in
          cross-section: shafts, and shadows between them.
          */
          val scene = PathTraceScene().apply {
              val floor = material(PathTraceMaterial.diffuse(0.32f, 0.30f, 0.27f))
              val wall = material(PathTraceMaterial.diffuse(0.16f, 0.17f, 0.21f))
              val slat = material(PathTraceMaterial.diffuse(0.10f, 0.09f, 0.08f))
              val lamp = material(PathTraceMaterial.emissive(340f, 300f, 230f))
              val ball = material(PathTraceMaterial.plastic(0.78f, 0.76f, 0.72f, 0.30f))
              quad(Vector3f(-6f, 0f, -4f), Vector3f(-6f, 0f, 4f), Vector3f(6f, 0f, 4f), Vector3f(6f, 0f, -4f), floor)
              quad(Vector3f(-6f, 0f, -4f), Vector3f(-6f, 5.4f, -4f), Vector3f(6f, 5.4f, -4f), Vector3f(6f, 0f, -4f), wall)
              quad(
                  Vector3f(-0.16f, 4.9f, -3.6f),
                  Vector3f(0.16f, 4.9f, -3.6f),
                  Vector3f(0.16f, 4.9f, 3.6f),
                  Vector3f(-0.16f, 4.9f, 3.6f),
                  lamp,
              )
              for (x in [-1.75f, -0.62f, 0.62f, 1.75f]) {
                  quad(
                      Vector3f(x - 0.26f, 3.5f, -3.6f),
                      Vector3f(x + 0.26f, 3.5f, -3.6f),
                      Vector3f(x + 0.26f, 3.5f, 3.6f),
                      Vector3f(x - 0.26f, 3.5f, 3.6f),
                      slat,
                  )
              }
              sphere(Vector3f(1.5f, 0.85f, 0.6f), 0.85f, ball, 40, 20)
          }
          val camera = Camera(renderer).also {
              it.at.set(0.15f, 2.35f, 9.2f)
              it.target.set(0.15f, 2.25f, 0f)
              it.p.fov = 0.82
          }
          tracer = PathTracingRenderer(
              renderer,
              scene,
              PathTraceEnvironment.constant(0f),
              800,
              500,
              camera,
              name = "medium-demo",
          )
          tracer.maxBounces = 8
          tracer.samplesPerFrame = 2
          tracer.showEnvironment = false
          tracer.background = Vector4f(0f, 0f, 0f, 1f)
          tracer.exposure = 0.22f

          /*
          ---- the medium. Bounds matter: an unbounded medium has zero transmittance to
          ---- infinity, which would make an environment map unreachable. Here the box is
          ---- the room, so rays leaving it are simply out of the haze.
          */
          tracer.mediumBounds = Vector3f(-6f, 0f, -3.9f) to Vector3f(6f, 5.2f, 3.9f)
          tracer.mediumAlbedo = Vector3f(0.96f, 0.95f, 0.93f)
          tracer.mediumAnisotropy = 0.4f
          tracer.mediumDensity = 0.16f

          tracer.install()
          tracer.blitToScreen()
          println(
              "${tracer.emitterCount} emissive triangles of ${tracer.triangleCount}; " +
                  "the medium is ${tracer.mediumDensity} per world unit, albedo ${tracer.mediumAlbedo}, " +
                  "g ${tracer.mediumAnisotropy}",
          )

          /*
          ---- MOVE THIS ONE PARAMETER: mediumDensity. -----------------------------------
          The loop cycles it every 192 samples and prints the value. At 0.0 you get the room
          with hard-edged pools of light on the floor and nothing in the air. As it rises the
          shafts between the slats appear, the lamp gains a halo, and the far wall goes soft.
          Past about 0.35 the haze starts to swallow the geometry -- and because every collision
          spends one of maxBounces, the image also darkens there unless you raise it.

          Try mediumAnisotropy next: 0.8 pulls the glow into a tight forward halo around the
          lamp, -0.8 throws it back toward the camera and flattens the shafts.
          Comment out the frames block to hold one setting.
          */
          frames {
              while (true) {
                  for (density in [0.0f, 0.08f, 0.16f, 0.40f]) {
                      tracer.mediumDensity = density
                      println("mediumDensity = $density")
                      // Changing it resets accumulation, but not until the next frame is recorded,
                      // so wait for the old budget to fall away before waiting for the new one.
                      while (tracer.samples >= 192) frame()
                      while (tracer.samples < 192) frame()
                  }
              }
          }
  - connect: { parent: pt_renderer, child: pt_medium }
  - launch: { box: pt_renderer, property: code, strand: renderer }
  - await: {}
  - execute: { box: pt_medium, property: code }
  - await: {}

before:
name: pattern_condense
description: >
  The shortest way to write a rhythm down. Three boxes: four rhythms drawn against their own
  condensations, a live check that the search invents no structure that is not there, and the
  loop closed from audio — samples in, a named figure out.

  `patCondense` searches Field's own mini-notation for the shortest string that plays the
  rhythm it is given, and it accepts a candidate only by playing it: every one goes back
  through `pat(...)` and its events are compared to the target's. That is why box 1 draws
  pairs rather than printing strings — the lower lane of a pair IS the string in its label,
  rendered, so a search that is wrong shows up as two lanes that do not coincide.

  Every box puts each output on its own channel. That is not decoration: boxes 1 and 3
  originally wrote the roll and then the table both to `main`, and the second silently
  overwrote the first, so the figure — the whole point — was never visible. Two writes to one
  channel is not an error, which is why nothing caught it and opening the document did.

  The saved document at `dev_docs/agents/demos/pattern_condense/` is this same scene. See `dev_docs/PAT_CONDENSE.md` and the section on
  `public/docs/pattern_language.md`.
operations:
  - create:
      box: condense_basics
      name: 1 - Condense a rhythm
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 60.0, w: 400.0, h: 136.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          1 - Condense a rhythm.

          patCondense searches Field's own mini-notation for the shortest string that plays the
          rhythm you hand it, and it accepts a candidate only by playing it: every one goes back
          through pat(...) and its events are compared to the target's. So the lower lane of each
          pair below IS the string in its label, rendered. If a pair does not coincide, the search
          is wrong, and that is a thing to see rather than a thing to be told.

          POKE THIS: change a line in `rhythms`, or add one. A mask you invent comes back either as
          a named figure - x(p,s) for Euclidean, x(kN) / x(gN) for Kolakoski - or spelled out, and
          which one you get is decided by character count and nothing else.
          */
          val rhythms = listOf(
              "x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~",
              "x ~ ~ x x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ ~ x x ~ x",
              "bd [hh hh] sd [cp cp]",
              "a b c d e c a d",
          )

          val found = showPatCondense(*rhythms.toTypedArray(), channel = "roll")

          val rows =
              rhythms.zip(found).joinToString("\n") { (source, c) ->
                  "| `$source` | `${c.notation}` | ${c.notation.length}/${c.flat.length} | " +
                      "${"%.2f".format(c.compression)} | ${c.structure.joinToString(", ")} |"
              }

          markdown(
              "main",
              """
              ### ${found.count { it.exact }} of ${found.size} condensed exactly

              | given | shortest string that plays it | chars | ratio | structure |
              |---|---|---|---|---|
              $rows

              The last row is why the other three mean anything. `a b c d e c a d` has no repeat at any
              split the grammar can take, so nothing shortens it and it comes back as itself. A search
              scored on description length has to be shown *not* naming a figure as well as naming one.

              Bounds this run used: ${found.first().limits}

              The figure is on the **roll** channel beside this one. These rhythms are abstract — `x`,
              `bd`, `a` — so there is nothing to play here; box 3 is the one you can listen to.
              """
                  .trimIndent(),
          )
  - create:
      box: condense_invents_nothing
      name: 2 - Invent nothing
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 500.0, w: 400.0, h: 136.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import kotlin.random.Random

          /*
          2 - Invent nothing.

          The failure mode of a description-length search is naming a figure that is one step away
          from the rhythm in front of it. This box runs that check live, on masks with no structure
          put into them.

          POKE THIS: change `seed`, or `density` (one step in N is on), or `trials`. The count of
          wrong namings has to stay 0 whatever you set, because every mask that came back as a
          whole-span figure is recomputed here from bjorklund / kolakoskiMask and compared.
          */
          val seed = 20260910
          val density = 3
          val trials = 300

          val random = Random(seed)
          val euclidean = Regex("""^x\((\d+),(\d+)(?:,(\d+))?\)$""")
          val kolakoskian = Regex("""^x\(([kg])(\d+)(?:,(\d+))?\)$""")

          var named = 0
          var wrong = 0
          val ratios = mutableListOf<Double>()

          repeat(trials) {
              val mask = List(16) { random.nextInt(density) == 0 }
              val condensed = patCondense(mask)
              ratios += condensed.compression
              euclidean.matchEntire(condensed.notation)?.let { m ->
                  named++
                  val pulses = m.groupValues[1].toInt()
                  val steps = m.groupValues[2].toInt()
                  val offset = m.groupValues[3].ifEmpty { "0" }.toInt()
                  val figure = List(steps) { i -> bjorklund(pulses, steps)[((i + offset) % steps + steps) % steps] }
                  if (figure != mask) wrong++
              }
              kolakoskian.matchEntire(condensed.notation)?.let { m ->
                  named++
                  val reading = if (m.groupValues[1] == "k") KolakoskiReading.RUNS else KolakoskiReading.GAPS
                  val steps = m.groupValues[2].toInt()
                  val offset = m.groupValues[3].ifEmpty { "0" }.toInt()
                  if (kolakoskiMask(steps, reading, rotation = -offset) != mask) wrong++
              }
          }

          val median = ratios.sorted()[ratios.size / 2]
          val structured = patCondense(kolakoskiMask(16)).compression

          markdown(
              "main",
              """
              ### $trials random 16-step masks, seed $seed, one step in $density on

              | | |
              |---|---|
              | read as a single whole-span figure | **$named** |
              | of those, wrong | **$wrong** |
              | median compression | ${"%.3f".format(median)} |
              | the same number for `kolakoskiMask(16)` | ${"%.3f".format(structured)} |

              Noise compresses about ${"%.1f".format(median / structured)} times worse than the figure
              it is up against. That separation is the claim. If random masks compressed as well as
              structured ones, the search would be finding figures in nothing.

              None of this rests on the search's own opinion of itself: every string it returned was
              re-parsed and re-played before it was accepted, and the namings above are recomputed from
              the generators rather than read off the label.
              """
                  .trimIndent(),
          )
  - create:
      box: condense_from_audio
      name: 3 - Close the loop
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 940.0, w: 400.0, h: 136.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          3 - Close the loop: samples in, structure out.

          patTranscribe recovers a step grid from audio and writes it out one slot per step, which
          is as far as listening alone can go. patCondense takes that string and returns the figure.
          So this box renders a bar to samples, throws the pattern away, listens to the samples, and
          gets the structure back.

          POKE THIS: change `bar`. Anything on an eight-step grid at MIDI 60 will be heard. Try
          "60 ~ ~ 60 60 ~ 60 ~", which comes back as 60(k8), or "60 60 ~ 60 ~ ~ 60 ~", which has no
          single figure and comes back as two halves.
          */
          val bar = "60 ~ ~ 60 ~ 60 ~ ~"

          val audio = patRenderStereo(
              pat(bar),
              cycles = 1,
              cps = 0.5,
              voice = patVoice(decay = 0.06, sustain = 0.6),
          )
          val heard = patTranscribe(audio.mono, PatSoundDocs.SR, minHz = 180.0, maxHz = 420.0)
          val condensed = patCondense(heard)

          showPatRollOf(
              "played" to pat(bar),
              "heard" to pat(heard.miniNotation),
              "condensed: ${condensed.notation}" to pat(condensed.notation),
              title = "audio in, structure out",
              subtitle = "${audio.mono.size} samples at ${PatSoundDocs.SR} Hz, and no knowledge of what made them",
              cycles = 1,
              channel = "roll",
          )

          /*
          The two players are the claim you can hear. The first is the EXACT buffer patTranscribe was
          given - not a re-render of `bar`, the same floats - so what you hear is what was listened to.
          The second is `condensed.notation` sent back through the same voice. If patCondense is right
          they are the same bar, and the point of a shortest notation is that shortening it cost nothing.
          */
          display(
              "played",
              afield.audio.engine.WavFloatArrayWriter.encodeStereo16(
                  audio.left,
                  audio.right,
                  PatSoundDocs.SR,
                  normalizePeak = 0.9f,
              ),
          )
          showPatAudio(
              pat(condensed.notation),
              cycles = 1,
              cps = 0.5,
              voice = patVoice(decay = 0.06, sustain = 0.6),
              channel = "condensed",
          )

          markdown(
              "main",
              """
              ### From samples to a figure

              | | |
              |---|---|
              | played | `$bar` |
              | rendered | ${audio.mono.size} samples, ${"%.2f".format(audio.mono.size.toDouble() / PatSoundDocs.SR)} s |
              | grid recovered | ${heard.grid?.describe() ?: "none"} |
              | heard | `${heard.miniNotation}` |
              | **condensed** | **`${condensed.notation}`** |

              The `heard` row is everything `patTranscribe` can say on its own. The last row is the same
              bar after `patCondense(heard)`, and it names the figure. Nothing between the render and the
              transcription looked at `bar`.

              Four outputs, each on its own channel: **roll** draws the three lanes, **played** is the
              buffer that was actually transcribed, **condensed** is `${condensed.notation}` rendered
              back through the same voice, and this table is **main**. The two players should be the
              same bar — that is the claim, and it is the one part of this box you can check by ear.
              """
                  .trimIndent(),
          )
  - launch: { box: condense_basics, property: code }
  - launch: { box: condense_invents_nothing, property: code }
  - launch: { box: condense_from_audio, property: code }
  - await: { wait: pending }

              "sine().rev()" to sine().segment(8).rev().texts(),

              subtitle = "the midpoint convention is what makes rev() line up",

          displayOpen("live")

              "segment(4) arcs = " + sine().segment(4).events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { "${it.arc}" },

              "segment(4) values = " + sine().segment(4).events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { "%.4f".format(it.value) },
          )
  # 2 ── structure choice: the operator family, and the event tables it produces.

      box: pat_demo_structure
      name: 2 — whose rhythm survives
      frame: { x: 820.0, y: 60.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // When two patterns meet, one of three things happens to the rhythm. The bars say where
          // the structure comes from, exactly as in Tidal.

          val threes = pat("10 20 30").nums()

          showPatRoll("structure-choice")
          displayOpen("main")

          // A lambda, not a named `fun`: K2 cannot codegen a named function inside a box that
          // captures the script's implicit Box receiver (which `println` needs).
          val table = { label: String, p: PatPattern<Double> ->
              val events = p.events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }
              println(
                  "%-10s %d events  %s"
                      .format(
                          label,
                          events.size,
                          events.joinToString(" ") { "[${it.arc.start}..${it.arc.end}]=${patFormatNumber(it.value)}" },
                      ),
              )
          }
          table("|+| both", twos.`|+|`(threes)) // 4 events: the intersection grid
          table("|+ left", twos.`|+`(threes)) // 2 events: exactly the left's
          table("+| right", twos.`+|`(threes)) // 3 events: exactly the right's

          // `/`, `<` and `>` are illegal in a Kotlin identifier, so division is `|over|` and the
          // take-value family spells the arrow as an L or an R. The bar keeps its Tidal meaning.
          table("|over|", twos.`|over|`(threes))

              "bd sd `#` x y z w = " + (pat("bd sd").`#`(pat("x y z w"))).events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { it.value },
          )
  # 3 ── the counterfactual: a continuous parameter without multiplying the notes.
  - create:
      box: pat_demo_parameter
      name: 3 — a parameter, not a staircase
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 520.0, w: 330.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          Before tonight the only way to attach a value to an atom was zip(...) with a string
          pattern: one literal per note, typed by hand. Now a parameter can be a FUNCTION, and
          the note count does not change when you read it.
          */
          showPatRoll("continuous-parameter")
          displayOpen("main")

          val curve = sine().rangex(300, 6000)
          for (n in listOf(4, 8, 16)) {
              val notes =
                  (pat("45*$n") with cutoff(curve)).events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }
              println(
                  "bd*%-2d -> %2d notes, cutoff %s"
                      .format(
                          n,
                          notes.size,
                          notes.joinToString(" ") { "%.0f".format(it.num("cutoff")) },
                      ),
              )
          }
          // appBoth is the other choice: it intersects both sides, so a 16-step sweep cuts
          // each note where the curve steps:
          println(
              "appBoth against a 16-step sweep -> " +
                  pat("45*4").appBoth(curve.segment(16)) { a, _ -> a }.events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).size +
                  " events",
          )

          // Hear it: a 110 Hz saw whose filter follows the curve, one value latched per note.
          showPatAudio(
              pat("45*16") with cutoff(curve) with gain(0.7),
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 2.0,
              voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.SAW, baseHz = 110.0, decay = 0.012, sustain = 0.3),
              channel = "sound",
          )
          displayOpen("sound")
  # 4 ── the flagship listen: two cycles flat, two cycles following an LFO.
  - create:
      box: pat_demo_gain
      name: 4 — hear the difference
      frame: { x: 820.0, y: 520.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          Sixteen hats a cycle. `whenCycle` is the existing operator for "from cycle 2 on, play
          this instead", so the first half of the file is what the old surface could express and
          the second half is the identical pattern with the gain following a sine.
          */

          val demo = hats.whenCycle({ it >= 2 }) { hats with gain(sine().range(0.08, 1.0)) }

          showPatRollOf(
              "flat (cycles 0-1)" to hats,
              "gain(sine()) (cycles 2-3)" to (hats with gain(sine().range(0.08, 1.0))),
              title = "the same sixteen hats, before and after",
              subtitle = "rectangle height is the gain each note latched",
              cycles = 2,
              paramKey = "gain",
          )
          displayOpen("main")

          val audio = showPatAudio(
              demo,
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 2.0,
              voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.NOISE, decay = 0.006, sustain = 0.05),
              channel = "sound",
          )
          displayOpen("sound")

          // The same measurement the smoke test makes, live: per-note level, flat then modulated.
          val onsets = PatSoundDocs.onsetPeaks(audio.mono)
          val flat = onsets.take(onsets.size / 2).map { it.rms }
          val modulated = onsets.drop(onsets.size / 2).map { it.rms }
          println("${onsets.size} hats detected")
          println("flat half level CV      = %.4f".format(PatSoundDocs.variation(flat)))
          println("modulated half level CV = %.4f".format(PatSoundDocs.variation(modulated)))
  # 5 ── the pitch surface, and the part Tidal has no answer for.
  - create:
      box: pat_demo_voice_leading
      name: 5 — voice leading
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 1020.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // Spelled from each chord's own root, a progression makes the hand leap. voiceLead()
          // picks each chord's inversion and octave to minimise how far the voices have to move.
          val progression = chords("c'maj7 a'min7 d'min7 g'dom7")
          val asWritten = progression.events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }.map { it.value }
          val voiceLed =
              progression
                  .voiceLead(center = 60)
                  .events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE))
                  .sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }
                  .map { it.value }

          displayOpen("main")

          println("voice-led  : $voiceLed")
          println(
              "movement   : %.0f semitones as written, %.0f voice-led"
                  .format(
                      patTotalVoiceMovement(asWritten),
                      patTotalVoiceMovement(voiceLed),
                  ),
          )

              "harmony unchanged: " +
                  asWritten.zip(voiceLed).all { (a, b) ->
                      a.map { Math.floorMod(it, 12) }.toSortedSet() == b.map { Math.floorMod(it, 12) }.toSortedSet()
                  },
          )

          // Hear both: two cycles as written, two voice-led.
          val arped = progression.arpeggiate().texts()
          val led = progression.voiceLead(center = 60).arpeggiate().texts()

              arped.whenCycle({ it >= 2 }) { led },
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 1.0,
              voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.SINE, decay = 0.02, sustain = 0.45),
              channel = "sound",
          )
          displayOpen("sound")
  # 6 ── the box to edit: a whole groove from the arrangement surface.
  - create:
      box: pat_demo_playground
      name: 6 — playground (edit me)
      frame: { x: 820.0, y: 1020.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // A little piece. Change any string or any number and re-run this box: the roll and the
          // audio player both come from the same pattern, so they can never disagree.
          val kick = struct(euclid(3, 8), pat("bd"))
          val snare = pat("~ sd ~ sd") with gain(0.8)
          val hats = pat("hh*16?0.3") with gain(sine().range(0.1, 0.55))
          val drums = stack(kick, snare, hats).off(1, 16) { it with gain(0.18) }

          // A bass line spelled in a scale, with a filter that opens across two cycles.
          val bass = run(8).scale("minPent", root = 36).texts().with(sustain(0.5), cutoff(saw().rangex(200, 2400)))

          // A chord pad, voice-led so it does not leap, arpeggiated up.
          val pad = chords("<c'min7 a'maj7> f'maj7").voiceLead(center = 67).arpeggiate().texts()

          showPatRollOf(
              "drums" to drums,
              "bass" to bass,
              "pad" to pad,
              title = "a groove, from the arrangement surface",
              subtitle = "euclid / off / ?degrade / scale / voiceLead / arpeggiate",
              cycles = 2,
          )
          displayOpen("main")

          showPatAudio(
              drums,
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 2.0,
              voice = patVoice(decay = 0.01, sustain = 0.08),
              channel = "drums",
          )
          showPatAudio(
              bass,
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 2.0,
              voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.SAW, decay = 0.03, sustain = 0.5),
              channel = "bass",
          )
          showPatAudio(
              pad,
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 2.0,
              voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.TRIANGLE, decay = 0.05, sustain = 0.6),
              channel = "pad",
          )
          displayOpen("drums")
          displayOpen("bass")
          displayOpen("pad")

          println("drums: ${drums.events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).size} events/cycle")
          println("bass : ${bass.events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { it.value }}")
          println("pad  : ${pad.events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { it.value }}")
  # 7 ── groove: swing you can hear, and the substitution primitive.
  - create:
      box: pat_demo_groove
      name: 7 — groove and substitution
      frame: { x: 60.0, y: 1560.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          // swing() is exact rational time, not a nudge in milliseconds: every off-beat lands a
          // third of a subdivision late and the pattern stays exactly quantised.
          val hats = pat("hh*8")
          showPatRoll("groove")
          displayOpen("main")

          println("straight : " + hats.events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { "${it.arc.start}" })
          println(
              "swing(4) : " +
                  hats
                      .swing(4)
                      .events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE))
                      .sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }
                      .map { "${it.arc.start}" },
          )

          // squeeze replaces each event with a whole pattern, compressed into that event's arc —
          // mini-notation nesting, over Kotlin values. Compare `join`, which does not rescale.
          val nested = pat("a b").squeeze { if (it == "a") pat("1 2 3") else pat("4 5") }
          println(
              "squeeze  : " +
                  nested
                      .events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE))
                      .sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }
                      .map { "${it.value}@${it.arc.start}" },
          )

          // Two cycles straight, then two swung. This is the one to listen to.
          showPatAudio(
              hats.whenCycle({ it >= 2 }) { hats.swing(4) },
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 2.0,
              voice = patVoice(wave = PatWave.NOISE, decay = 0.008, sustain = 0.06),
              channel = "swing",
          )
          displayOpen("swing")

          // And a full bar from one Euclidean figure: bd on the onsets, hh on everything else.
          showPatAudio(
              euclidFull(3, 8, pat("bd"), pat("hh") with gain(0.35)),
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 2.0,
              voice = patVoice(decay = 0.012, sustain = 0.1),
              channel = "euclid",
          )
          displayOpen("euclid")
  # 8 ── mini-notation: the step markers, seen and heard against their bracketed equivalents.
  - create:
      box: pat_demo_mini_notation
      name: 8 — mini-notation markers
      frame: { x: 820.0, y: 1560.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          Three standalone step markers. Each is shorthand for a bracketed form, so each pair
          below must come out arc-for-arc identical — and the roll draws them one above the other
          so you can check by eye as well as by assertion.
          */
          showPatRoll("mini-notation")
          displayOpen("main")

          val pairs = listOf(
              "bd sd . hh hh hh" to "[bd sd] [hh hh hh]", // `.` groups
              "bd _ _ sd" to "bd@3 sd", // `_` extends
              "bd ! ! sd" to "bd!3 sd", // bare `!` repeats
          )
          for ((shorthand, bracketed) in pairs) {
              val a = pat(shorthand).events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }
              val b = pat(bracketed).events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).sortedBy { it.arc.start.toDouble() }
              val same = a.map { it.arc } == b.map { it.arc } && a.map { it.value } == b.map { it.value }
              println(
                  "%-20s == %-22s : %s   %s"
                      .format(
                          shorthand,
                          bracketed,
                          same,
                          a.joinToString(" ") { "${it.value}@${it.arc.start}" },
                      ),
              )
          }

          // A `.` inside a token is still part of the token — decimals and sample payloads are safe.
          println(
              "0.5 1.25 -> " + pat("0.5 1.25").nums().events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { it.value },
          )
          println("my_atom  -> " + pat("my_atom b").events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).map { it.value })

          // A sample-index suffix becomes an `n` parameter without changing the atom.
          pat("bd:3 sd 808:12").events(PatArc(PatQ.ZERO, PatQ.ONE)).forEach {
              println("atom ${it.value} -> n=${it.annotations["n"]}, span=\"${it.sourceSpan?.text}\"")
          }

          // Hear the dot: two cycles of five even notes, then the same five notes grouped.
          showPatAudio(
              pat("bd sd hh hh hh").whenCycle({ it >= 2 }) { pat("bd sd . hh hh hh") },
              cycles = 4,
              cps = 1.0,
              voice = patVoice(decay = 0.012, sustain = 0.12),
              channel = "dot",
          )
          displayOpen("dot")
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_signals }
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_structure }
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_parameter }
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_gain }
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_voice_leading }
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_playground }
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_groove }
  - execute: { box: pat_demo_mini_notation }
